articles.title: The Longest Active Championship Droughts in Sports After Brewers Win World Series
articles.summary: Apparently, 2026 is the year of snapping long championship droughts.
articles.body:
Apparently, 2026 is the year of snapping long championship droughts.

In June, the New York Knicks won their first title in 53 years after defeating the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals. Four months later, the Milwaukee Brewers snapped a 57-year championship drought by beating the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series.

Winning a title is the goal for every professional team. Every addition to and subtraction from the roster is made with a long-term vision in mind. Even an intentional teardown is executed with the idea of building up a future contender.

But as the Knicks and Brewers know full well, a championship can be agonizingly elusive. For some organizations, the dream of winning a title has never been more than exactly that.

In the wake of the Knicks' and Brewers' wins, the following teams now have the longest championship droughts across all of the major U.S. sports.

On the heels of a drought-snapping postseason berth in 2026, a jolt of excitement has surged through the Buffalo Sabres' fanbase.

Prior to that 15-year absence, the Sabres had been a playoff mainstay. Buffalo made its NHL debut in 1970 and earned a ticket to the postseason 29 times throughout its first 40 years, making two runs to the Stanley Cup Final.

In both 1975 and 1999, the Philadelphia Flyers and Dallas Stars, respectively, dispatched the Sabres in six games.

Perhaps a championship window is starting to open in Buffalo, though.

Meanwhile, the vibes are extraordinarily low around the Vancouver Canucks, who just finished the recent NHL season as the worst team in the league. Adding salt to the wound, they dropped to third in the 2026 draft.

In their 55-year history, though, the Canucks have enjoyed a few periods of sustained success and reached the Stanley Cup Final on three occasions.

And they've been so tantalizingly close to hoisting the Cup.

Vancouver lost to the New York Islanders in a four-game sweep in 1982. Later, both the New York Rangers and Boston Bruins toppled the Canucks in Game 7 showdowns during the 1994 and 2011 playoffs, respectively.

Every iteration of this franchise—the Buffalo Braves in 1970 to the San Diego Clippers in 1978 to the Los Angeles Clippers in 1984—has fallen short of winning a championship.

That's a short-and-sweet, blunt summary.

Prior to their "Lob City" ascent in 2011, the Clippers reached the playoffs in just seven of their first 41 seasons. Los Angeles picked No. 1 overall more times (three) than it won playoff series (two) during that stretch.

In the last 15 years, L.A. has established itself as an annual playoff team. Yet those 12 appearances have resulted in a lone Western Conference Finals run.

The next time the Clippers make the NBA Finals will be their first.

Way-Too-Early Predictions for 2027 MLB Playoffs 🔮

Another part of MLB's expansion in 1969, the San Diego Padres experienced a slow start to their professional journey.

In the first 15 years of existence, the Padres never finished better than fourth in the NL West—and only division winners made the playoffs. They finally broke through in 1984 and advanced to the World Series, losing to the Detroit Tigers in five games.

San Diego returned to the Fall Classic in 1998 but endured a sweep by the dynasty-era New York Yankees.

Since then, the Pads have managed just six postseason berths and have made only a single appearance in the NLCS in 2022.

Cleveland's tortured sports history is riddled with angst. (At least the Cavaliers won in 2016, right?)

The city's main gripe is that the Browns have stunk for 30-plus years.

Incidentally, that wasn't the case early on. During the pre-Super Bowl days, the franchise won four AAFC championships and three NFL titles in a 10-year period. Cleveland won the 1964 NFL championship, too.

The organization was also competent in the 1980s with seven playoff bids.

Since the 1990 season, though—even excluding the 1996–98 seasons when operations were suspended—the Browns have made only four playoff appearances and have not reached the AFC Championship Game.

Congratulations are due to the New York Jets. They're the organization with the longest title drought to last win a championship under its current name.

Joe Namath memorably led the heavy-underdog Jets to a Super Bowl triumph in 1969, knocking off the Baltimore Colts.

Unfortunately for the Jets, they haven't soared to those same heights ever since. Among their 13 playoff appearances since then, the Jets reached the AFC Championship Game four times but dropped each one.

Heading into the 2026 season, the NFL's longest postseason drought—at 15 years—belongs to the Jets.

Two seasons after the Super Bowl era kicked off, the Cincinnati Bengals joined the AFL party (1968) shortly before the AFL-NFL merger (1970).

Cincy rose to prominence in the 1980s, winning the AFC in 1981 and 1988 with Ken Anderson and Boomer Esiason, respectively, at quarterback. However, the Joe Montana-led San Francisco 49ers won both Super Bowl matchups.

Then, in February 2022, another NFC West franchise took down the Bengals in the Super Bowl.

Cooper Kupp's late touchdown catch pushed the Los Angeles Rams to a 23-20 win in their own stadium, sending Cincy home empty-handed.

One of the "Original Six" NHL teams, the Toronto Maple Leafs have a proud history and a passionate fanbase.

They just haven't had much to celebrate for a long, long time.

The Maple Leafs have won 13 NHL titles in their 108-year history, but their last one came in 1966-67. They haven't even been back to the Stanley Cup Final since then.

They've made the postseason 36 times over that span, but they've repeatedly failed to break through.

As if that's not enough, through the 2025-26 campaign, Toronto is riding a 24-year drought of making the conference finals, let alone the Cup.

Since the Super Bowl era began with the 1966 season, seven franchises have played every NFL season without winning a Super Bowl.

Easily one of the more painful extended droughts, the Buffalo Bills hold the inglorious honor of losing four straight Super Bowls. They boasted a Hall of Fame-filled roster but lost in the 1990, 1991, 1992 and 1993 seasons.

Similarly, the Minnesota Vikings (1969, 1973, 1974 and 1976) have fallen short in their four attempts at the Lombardi Trophy.

Each of the Arizona Cardinals (2008), Atlanta Falcons (1998 and 2016) and Tennessee Titans (1999) endured soul-crushing losses. Arizona lost on a last-minute touchdown, Atlanta infamously blew a 28-3 lead in 2016, and Tennessee fell a literal yard short of a ring.

Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Chargers suffered a blowout defeat at Super Bowl XXIX in January 1995.

Rounding out this group in the most frustrating fashion is the Detroit Lions , who have yet to appear in a Super Bowl.

Initially known as the Tri-Cities Blackhawks and Milwaukee Hawks, the St. Louis Hawks won an NBA title in 1958. The team then moved to Georgia in 1968.

The Atlanta Hawks have become an exhausting team to support ever since.

Unlike our next NBA organization, Atlanta has consistently been a competitive team. Within this extended drought, the Hawks have reached the playoffs in 46 of those campaigns—essentially two-thirds of the time.

The problem is that most of their postseason runs have ended quickly.

Since moving to Atlanta, only two years included a spot in the conference finals—with zero NBA Finals trips.

As the Rochester Royals, the organization wasted no time making its mark. It celebrated an NBA title in 1951, just three seasons after joining the NBA's predecessor, the BAA.

The franchise moved to become the Cincinnati Royals in 1957, relocated as the Kansas City (Omaha) Kings in 1972 and became the Sacramento Kings in 1985.

Over these four decades, the Kings had an eight-year stretch of contention from 1999-2006 and little else.

Save for brief postseason stays in 1986, 1996 and 2023, the Kings haven't made the playoffs except in their era with players like Mike Bibby, Chris Webber, Peja Stojaković and Vlade Divac. Sacramento never made an NBA Finals in that stretch, only reaching one Western Conference Finals.

Since the franchise last won a World Series back in 1948, Cleveland has returned to the championship stage four times, only to come up empty each time.

First, it was a sweep at the hands of the New York Giants (1954). Following a four-decade playoff drought, it was a six-game loss to the Atlanta Braves (1995) and crushing seven-game series loss to the Florida Marlins (1997).

Most recently, it was a soul-crushing collapse to the Chicago Cubs (2016). Cleveland squandered a 3-1 series lead and lost Game 7 at home in extra innings.

articles.title: Fantasy football rookie WR check-in: Rest-of-season outlook for every key first-year receiver
articles.summary: Matt Harmon checks in on the rookie wide receiver class, offering fantasy managers a rest-of-season outlook for more than 20 players.
articles.body:
Matt Harmon checks in on the 2026 NFL rookie wide receiver class, grouping players by usage to help fantasy football managers gauge their outlook for the rest of the season.

Denzel Boston, Browns: He has been the most productive rookie wide receiver this season. He has been an instant hit for Cleveland, following up on the promise foretold by a summer's worth of buzz from OTAs and training camp. What's most impressive about Boston's season is that he's done all his damage while lining up almost exclusively at X-receiver — his 6.3% slot rate is the lowest among all starting receivers in the NFL. He's had a strong connection with Deshaun Watson on targets outside the numbers in this role. While his production may be more volatile going forward if he sticks as a primary outside receiver, I expect him to finish with strong end-of-season numbers.

Carnell Tate, Titans: He was the first rookie wide receiver drafted and is just behind Boston in total fantasy production (60.3 to 67.2 points). Tate leads the class with 2.0 yards per route run, if you remove small sample-size wonders. He's done what you can ask out of a receiver playing in a bad offense with shaky quarterback play. Tate has dropped too many passes (8% drop rate) but made up for it with tight coverage contested wins. He has fantastic ball skills, and I'm not worried about small mistakes. The Titans offense won't allow him to fully flourish in fantasy this season but he's a hit for this team as a boundary receiver starter.

KC Concepcion, Browns: He had his long-overdue breakout game in Week 7 with 129 yards. He dropped a deep shot in a void in the Titans' cover-two shell, so it could have been an even bigger day. Concepcion has been targeted on 24.2% of his routes this season, most among guys who have played all season. Watson just finally hit him on some in-breakers in Week 7 that allowed his run-after-catch skills to shine. Concepcion looks like a future star on tape and I expect more big statistical days are on the horizon. The Browns hit a home run with their receiver draft picks.

Makai Lemon, Eagles: His full-season production doesn't look great. He's run a route on 87% of the Eagles' dropbacks this season but averages a paltry 0.86 yards per route. Everyone should have expected Lemon to start slow after a lost offseason with hamstring injuries. You can pencil in any rookie who misses huge chunks of camp time for a delayed lift-off. However, he's started to look better and is playing with more confidence on tape the last couple of weeks. This coincides with more opportunities as other Eagles wideouts miss time. Lemon has a clear runway to be a productive option, albeit in an offense that isn't nearly as well set up as what we typically imagine for Philadelphia.

Ted Hurst, Buccaneers: He has run a route on 66% of the Buccaneers' dropbacks this season. He's the team's primary X-receiver and the only option on the roster with the frame to handle those duties full time. However, Hurst is a raw rookie coming from Georgia State. You've seen the ups and downs that profile would suggest. He's unlikely to be consistently productive this season but I'll be tracking his progress in the back half.

Malachi Fields, Giants: He has run a route on 76% of the dropbacks for the Giants. He's averaging 35.3 yards per game but made a couple of huge plays with J.J. McCarthy in Week 7 on big out-breaking routes. I like Fields the most of this cohort, but he's a better real-life than fantasy player. The good news for fake gamers is that Fields can play all over the formation, including X, which lets the Giants move Malik Nabers around for layup matchups. When Nabers moves into the slot, he has averaged over 5.0 yards per route.

Bryce Lance, Saints: He has run a route on 79% of the Saints' dropbacks, trailing only Boston, Tate and Lemon among rookies. He's been targeted on just 9.4% of those routes, third-lowest among receivers to play over 200 snaps this year. Lance is a big body with tons of speed but he's primarily been a sacrificial option for New Orleans to clear space for his teammates. While he may have a bright future, I guess he'll eventually cede his spot to Round 1 rookie Jordyn Tyson. On that note…

Jordyn Tyson, Saints: He has yet to play this season but can be activated off IR at any time. The Saints are on bye in Week 8 after an international game, so my guess is that he starts to get ramped up ahead of Week 9. Tyson is a highly intriguing player who I believe fits the Saints' offensive scheme well, as they spread the field and get everyone reps off-ball and in the slot. It might be aggressive to expect him to step into a full-time role right away, considering he's missed so much time and these hamstring issues have been a massive problem all year. The Saints want to win and see their Round 1 pick thrive, but they also have a ton of incentive to make sure these issues don't crop up again, so they may approach with caution.

Germie Bernard, Steelers: He has run a route on over 97% of the Steelers' dropbacks the last three weeks after the team placed Michael Pittman on IR. The rookie has 20 catches on 26 targets during that timeframe. He's found a home as the big slot option for a team that needed a rugged, reliable option in the passing game. Bernard needs a ton of volume to produce in his current role but he has the trust of his quarterback, which hasn't often been bestowed on rookies.

Omar Cooper Jr., Jets: He came IR from a high ankle sprain suffered on an explosive play in Week 1 and has been fantastic. He has run out as the Jets' full-time WR2 the last two games and has cleared 100 yards in both contests. Cooper averages 4.77 yards per route run this season, which is obviously outrageous. Cooper's tape has been excellent and he's brought a new dimension to the Jets' offense. I expect him to remain a huge part of the offense and have more big weeks, even if he won't keep up this exact production. His receiver archetype is what's dominating the NFL at this position right now.

Caleb Douglas, Dolphins: He has only played three games but he returned in Week 7 and made an instant impact. He caught two passes and both went for touchdowns. He's shown an ability to separate at the top of his routes and looks as athletic as his testing would suggest. The Dolphins have some degree of a hit in their Round 3 selection.

Chris Bell, Dolphins: He tore his ACL late last year, so it's a feat that he's even playing at all. He's run a route on over 73% of the dropbacks the last four games. However, his rate dipped to 64% last week after Douglas returned. I'm expecting Bell to just get some development this year and come out as his best self in 2027 when he's a full year removed from his surgery.

Antonio Williams, Commanders: He should come out of the Commanders' Week 7 bye as a full-time player. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Washington needs juice and separation skills; Williams brings both. The team won't increase Stefon Diggs' playing time to preserve his body, so Williams should be a near every-down player. I love his tape so far and expect him to make a big post-bye impact.

Ja'Kobi Lane, Ravens: He is another rookie who left Week 1 with an injury but has returned for Baltimore's last two games. He ran a route on 58% of the dropbacks in Week 6 but jumped up to 75% last week. Lane is an X-receiver who brings size and ball skills that stand out in the Ravens room. He doesn't separate well, but he brings value in his role, especially because it lets their other receivers move around. I'm excited to see what he can do when Lamar Jackson gets back.

Josh Cameron, Jaguars: He has played on 35% of the Jaguars' snaps this season. He's mostly popped as a blocker but has earned a first down on 10.2% of his routes. There's something here. Cameron looks like a great dirty-work specialist, who could function as Jacksonville's WR3 in a rotation with Travis Hunter if the team trades Brian Thomas Jr.

Dohnte Meyers, Bengals: He is technically a rookie at 26 years old after playing in the CFL. He's run a route on 49% of the Bengals' dropbacks and had a few nice moments. He won't be a highly targeted option with the other stars in the room but the Bengals have needed some depth behind Higgins and Chase for years.

Kevin Coleman Jr., Dolphins: He is the third Dolphins receiver drafted this year. He has run a route on 51% of the team's dropbacks overall but dipped to 7.1% in Week 7 with Douglas back. For now, I view him as a backup to third-year slot starter Malik Washington, who has played well this season.

Zachariah Branch, Falcons: He has run a route on 27% of the Falcons' dropbacks this season but has only been used in a designed-touch role. He has caught 10 of 12 targets while averaging 2.08 air yards per target. As long as Drake London and Jahan Dotson stay healthy, there's not room for Branch to slice off much of the pie on a team that plays a lot of two-tight-end sets.

Cyrus Allen, Chiefs: He was one of my favorite Day 3 sleepers from this past year's draft and he got a ton of buzz in training camp for the Chiefs. He hasn't played much yet (32 snaps in six games) but has been targeted on a whopping 30% of his routes. Clearly, Patrick Mahomes likes him but Allen needs to get more up to speed with the playbook to earn more work. The Chiefs offense is notoriously hard for rookies to learn so we need to be patient here, but there's something worth waiting for with his game.

Deion Burks, Colts: He is another player I liked ahead of consensus and I was shocked he went off the board in Round 7. Burks wasn't super productive in college but is athletic and flashed playmaking ability. He's only run 29 routes but has earned a first down on nearly 14% of those and averages 23 air yards per target. He's a name to know for when the Colts trade Josh Downs in the coming days .

Zavion Thomas, Bears: He is likely to be a designed-touch threat only as a rookie but he brings a ton of juice and explosive play potential. My hunch when he was drafted was that he was destined to be Kalif Raymond's long-term replacement. Raymond held a big role for the team to start this season, so that's not nothing. Thomas is more of a dynasty name to know.

articles.title: The Milwaukee Brewers win the first World Series title in franchise history, defeating Tampa in 5 games
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers erased nearly six decades of heartache, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 to clinch the franchise’s first World Series title.
articles.body:
The Brewers are World Series champs! The Milwaukee Brewers have won the first World Series in franchise history, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday to complete a 4-1 series victory.

Milwaukee wins Game 5, 4-1: It was a perfectly small-ball way for the Brewers to win the title. RBI singles from Cooper Pratt and David Hamilton, a big double from William Contreras, key defensive plays by first baseman Jake Bauers and excellent pitching from ace Jacob Misiorowski.

Contreras named MVP: Brewers catcher William Contreras was named the World Series MVP after providing excellent work behind the plate as well as clutch hitting all series long.

History made: The Brewers had only been to one World Series before this year, losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.

Labor implications : The Brewers’ win is a victory for the league’s smallest media market and 19th-biggest payroll. Those facts will be brought up repeatedly in the labor fight to come before baseball’s collective bargaining agreement expires December 1.

Our live coverage of Game 5 of the World Series has ended. For a full recap of the Brewers’ World Series-clinching victory, read below.

The Milwaukee Brewers put on a masterclass in every facet of the game as they beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to win their first World Series title in franchise history in five games on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.

In a game that saw both teams’ aces go head-to-head, it was the Brewers’ Cy Young candidate Jacob Misiorowski besting Rays ace Drew Rasmussen.

The NL Cy Young frontrunner went five-and-two-thirds innings, striking out two while only allowing two hits before exiting the game with an apparent cramp in his leg. Rasmussen was pulled after four innings with him being on short rest and a reported pitch count of 60.

The real story was the Brewers offense – especially rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt.

Pratt got the scoring started in the second inning with an RBI single, scoring Brice Turang. And Milwaukee never looked back.

That wasn’t the only notable thing Pratt did – he made a little World Series history with his single. It was his sixth straight at-bat with a hit, the most for a rookie in Fall Classic history.

But it was the sixth inning when things went up a notch. William Contreras’ RBI double scored a run and then he would score on Pratt’s sacrifice fly to build the lead to 4-0.

The Rays bullpen was able to settle in, using seven total pitchers, but the Tampa offense was sound asleep until Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson both doubled in the ninth for the Rays, making the score 4-1.

Contreras was named the World Series MVP after batting .381 with four RBI.

The Brewers will now bring a World Series title back to Wisconsin.

For the first time in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions.

The Brew Crew dominated the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5, winning 4-1 in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Check out some of the best photos from the postgame celebrations:

It’s the last party of the season in a long line of them.

Every major US sport has multi-round postseason schedules, but none of them party like MLB teams. Locker room celebrations in the NFL tend to be subdued until the Super Bowl, and since hockey players are famously superstitious, popping bottles early is practically verboten in the NHL; the Stanley Cup is all that really matters.

Boston Red Sox clubhouse manager Tom McLaughlin has spent over 40 years with the Red Sox, and he says he’s lost track of how many celebrations he’s been involved in, but he counts them in the dozens. He told CNN Sports it was “pretty tame” when he started in the ‘80s, when the postseason was much shorter, but the back end of the season now can feel like one enormous bender for the most successful teams.

Successfully navigate the wildcard round? Let’s get wild.

Made it through the Divisional Round? Get another round in.

Won the Championship Series? We’re going on a spree.

By the time a baseball club wins the World Series , let’s just say that the celebration will not be their first rodeo. Everyone will have had plenty of practice.

Florida’s Natural, the juice giant from the Sunshine State, is about to pay up.

Florida’s Natural and Johnsonville, the famous sausage company from Wisconsin, made a bet before the World Series. If the Rays won, Johnsonville would be sending 400,000 bratwursts to Tampa Bay for victory grilling.

But the Rays came up short. So instead, Florida’s Natural will be sending north enough orange juice to make 200,000 mimosas, according to a news release from Johnsonville.

“We’ve been making 44 year to make this wager, so we’re going big,” said Jamie Schmelzer, the vice president of marketing at Johnsonville.

It’s a kid’s game played by grown men. But sometimes it’s nice to see that those men don’t lose sight of what it all means.

Trevor Megill closed out the game for the Brewers, getting the final six outs to clinch the World Series – a scenario that he dreamt about over and over.

“For the last two months or so, this is everything I could think of,” Megill told Fox. “You know, going to bed, coming to the field every single day. This moment right here.”

With a championship belt slung over his shoulder, Megill said: “This is just incredible, man. Ten-year-old me would be so proud.”

Brewers owner Mark Attanasio credited the city of Milwaukee and Brewers fans for their title win.

“Milwaukee has waited 44 years and Milwaukee you have your world championship,” Attanasio shouted.

Attanasio’s last words before celebrating more? “GO BREWERS!”

The Brewers’ star catcher William Contreras was named the MVP of the World Series, a well-deserved honor.

Contreras was excellent defensively behind the plate and made great use of his team Automatic Ball-Strike System challenges. He batted .381, knocked in four runs and was the spark plug for the team all series long.

“I don’t have words to say for how I’m feeling but I am just appreciative of my teammates. Appreciative of (Pat Murphy). I thank all of them,” Contreras said via his translator.

Contreras also called up star reliever Aaron Ashby, who was extremely complimentary of the catcher.

“He wants to compete every single day. He’d die for everyone on this team and he’d do anything for any of the guys on this team. He’s our bulldog and we love this dude,” Ashby said.

Milwaukee has waited 57 years for a World Series title. Cooper Pratt had to wait about four months.

Pratt, the Brewers shortstop who caught fire in this World Series at the plate, was called up to the Brewers in June. He found himself starting at shortstop in the Fall Classic just a few short months later and is now a champion.

“This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh,” he said, overwhelmed by the moment. “It doesn’t even feel real. Like, I don’t know. This is this is surreal. Only took four months!”

Pratt thanked Brewers fans and his teammates for being patient with him as he developed in the big leagues all season.

“The pressure is out of this world. It’s some of the hardest but most fun baseball I’ve ever been a part of,” he said. “I messed up a lot of times this postseason, but the guys picked. up, and we’re here, and we’re world champions. It’s so special, man. I’m so blessed.”

Bob Uecker spent 54 seasons as the voice of the Milwaukee Brewers, narrating every game every summer until his death in January 2025.

His loss was keenly felt in Wisconsin and throughout baseball as he was one of the game’s most well-known personalities.

Uecker died without ever seeing the Brewers win a World Series title, but Christian Yelich said he had a feeling that Ueck was watching on Wednesday.

“He’s smiling, man. He’s smiling. I really wish he could have been here to see this,” Yelich told the Fox broadcast. “But like we said, a bunch – he’s been with us a lot and we keep him close to our hearts. And you know, this one’s still for Bob. This is for Ueck.”

Ace and NL Cy Young award frontrunner Jacob Misiorowski was emotional after helping lead the Brewers to their first title in franchise history.

“I don’t even have words,” Misiorowski told the Fox broadcast. “You know, it’s amazing. Just watching my guys celebrate. In the city, I know they’re going crazy in Milwaukee. It’s awesome.”

Miz gave props to his catcher William Contreras for helping him handle the emotions throughout the season.

“We’ve been talking this whole week, and expecting this moment. … I couldn’t have done it without him, and it’s been amazing with him this whole season,” Misiorowski said.

Christian Yelich’s arrival in Milwaukee in 2018 marked a turning point for the franchise, making him the centerpiece of the next eras of Brewers baseball.

Yelich won the MVP that year and remained one of the biggest parts of the team, even as injuries robbed him of some of the production he had earlier in his career. With this title, he finally gets to call himself a World Series champion.

“I don’t even know how to describe it. It’s the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here,” Yelich told the Fox broadcast. “I know the city’s waited a long, long time for this, and we’re so happy to bring it home to them.

“Can’t wait to get back there and celebrate. I wish everybody could experience what this feels like. It feels amazing.”

The Milwaukee Brewers have erased nearly six decades of heartache, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 to clinch the franchise’s first World Series title.

The Brewers used their small-ball ways, leaning on clutch hitting, stellar defense and exquisite pitching from ace Jacob Misiorowski to claim Game 5 and win the title. It was a fitting exhibition of Brewers baseball that carried them to baseball’s best record in the regular season and saw them roll through the postseason.

RBI singles from Cooper Pratt and David Hamilton built the lead in the second and fifth innings, but it was the sixth when things went up a notch. William Contreras’ RBI double scored a run and then he would score on Pratt’s sacrifice fly to build the lead to 4-0.

Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson both doubled in the ninth for the Rays, making the score 4-1.

It’s an incredible moment for the city of Milwaukee’s baseball fans. The Brewers had only been to one World Series before this year, losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982. After coming within three outs of the title on Tuesday and falling short, the Brewers will get to go back to Milwaukee for a victory parade rather than Game 6.

The Brewers’ win is a victory for the league’s smallest media market and 19th-biggest payroll. Notably, the Brewers swept the big-money Los Angeles Dodgers to get to the World Series, a major bit of payback for a franchise has been building toward this moment for a decade.

Ian Seymour was the next man up from the Rays bullpen and was able to get the Brewers to go down 1-2-3 as their final chance to extend the World Series is now here.

After a disaster sixth inning for the Tampa bullpen, they have rebounded nicely despite using seven pitchers this game.

As we previously said, it was do-or-die time for the Rays as the Brewers are three outs from a title.

They have put so many balls in play tonight, including a ball hit 356 feet by Yandy Díaz with an expected batting average of .480 that turned into just a loud out when it was caught on the warning track.

But ultimately, they’re three outs away from going home empty handed and have yet to push a run across tonight.

It appears the Rays bullpen has finally settled in as Bryan Baker retired the heart of the Brewers’ lineup in order.

Heading into the bottom of the eighth inning, Tampa Bay needs to step on the gas offensively or they risk their season ending tonight.

Have you heard Chandler Simpson is fast?

Sure, there was an error on the play, but that’s because Simpson’s speed forced William Contreras to make a rushed throw on a swinging bunt that Statcast measured going just one foot.

Simpson wound up on second base after the throw sailed past the outstretched first baseman (and into the absurdly un-enclosed bullpen located in foul territory).

The runner in scoring position prompted the Brewers to bring in Abner Uribe, who got Richie Palacios to ground out on the first pitch. Victor Mesa, Jr. battles through a nine-pitch at bat, but ultimately he grounds out, too.

Rays are down to six outs to score at least four runs to save their season.

Despite a Jackson Chourio leadoff single – his 11th hit of the World Series – Steven Matz was able to make quick work of Jake Bauers and Christian Yelich to get out of the inning.

Rays batters will need to show some signs of life as they will be facing the battle-tested Brewers bullpen the rest of the way.

Just like that, Jacob Misiorowski’s night is over.

The Miz was on cruise control before getting Junior Caminero to fly out to right. He throws one pitch to Liam Hicks and it’s fouled off, and suddenly the Brewers’ trainer is coming out to the mound.

Misiorowski’s longest postseason start – his last appearance before winning the Cy Young award – would end prematurely with what appears to be a cramp.

It’s a shame, at just 86 pitches in the sixth inning, it would have been compelling to see how deep he could go.

But he left with a four-run lead and his team 10 outs from winning the World Series.

It didn’t take long for JoJo Romero to get out of the inning, getting Hicks to ground out to end the sixth. The Brewers are nine outs away from their first World Series title.

Cooper Pratt has been one of, if not the most important players on the Brewers this World Series.

After making history his previous at-bat, he looked to make it seven straight at-bats with a hit.

While it didn’t result in a hit, his sacrifice fly brought in Milwaukee’s fourth run of the game as things are unraveling for the Rays since Drew Rasmussen was taken out and the bullpen came in. Pratt’s 1.000 batting average in the last few games still stands.

The 22-year-old Pratt now has a team-high seven RBI’s this series.

Steven Matz was able to get David Hamilton to fly out to end the inning, stranding Brice Turang on third base.

Rays are running out of time to extend this series.

articles.title: ESPN anchor Hannah Storm announces she is cancer-free, but will miss NYC Marathon coverage while recovering from surgery
articles.summary: Storm has co-hosted coverage of the NYC Marathon since 2013.
articles.body:
ESPN anchor Hannah Storm posted to her X account on Wednesday that she is cancer-free.

Storm's announcement on Wednesday also included that she recently underwent a hysterectomy. She is recovering from the procedure, which will keep her out of work a little longer and mean she will miss covering this weekend's New York City Marathon.

The ESPN anchor is known for her annual NYC Marathon coverage, which will air Sunday morning. Storm has co-hosted coverage of the event since 2013.

Two years ago, during an appearance on "Good Morning America," the SportsCenter anchor revealed that she had been diagnosed with DCIS breast cancer. Storm had previously said that she underwent a lumpectomy on Feb. 1 of that year.

In her statement, Storm shouts out marathon runners supporting great causes like the Hannah Storm Foundation. She founded the foundation in 2008 to raise awareness and fund treatment for children with vascular abnormalities. Storm herself was born with this condition.

Storm's philanthropy doesn't end there. She is also notably involved in advocacy for burn survivors, after she had second-degree burns in a propane grill accident in 2012.

These efforts largely led to her winning the 2025 Pat Summerall Award, making her the second woman to receive it. The Pat Summerall Award is given "to honor a national broadcaster or prominent sports personality who exemplified the characteristics Pat Summerall wanted the award to represent — an individual who has had an outstanding career and who has made a significant impact in their community."

Storm is expected to make a full recovery and ended her statement saying, "See y'all soon on SportsCenter."

articles.title: “Not all girls, especially girls from underserved communities”: How Naomi Osaka’s initiative is helping girls with disabilities build confidence and become future sports leaders
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka wants more girls to experience the opportunities that sport gives her.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka wants more girls to experience the opportunities that sport gives her. Through Play Academy with Naomi Osaka, the four-time Grand Slam champion supports community organisations that help girls participate in sports and develop skills beyond the court. One example is NPO J Camp in Japan, where her initiative supports a project that gives girls with disabilities opportunities to play wheelchair basketball and explore leadership roles.The project, called Push for Future, began in 2024 with support from Play Academy. It gives Osaka’s wider mission a practical focus: helping girls build confidence through sport while creating opportunities for young women to guide the next generation.How Naomi Osaka’s Play Academy is expanding sports opportunities for girls with disabilitiesOsaka launched Play Academy in 2020 with Nike and Laureus Sport for Good. She drew on her own experience as a young tennis player and recognised that many girls do not have the same access to sport or role models.“I’ve been playing tennis since I was 3 years old, and it has changed my life. But I know not all girls, especially girls from underserved communities. have the same opportunities or role models that I’ve had, and I want to do something about it,” Osaka said in her statement on the official Play Academy website.Her initiative supports grassroots organisations rather than running every programme itself. In Japan, that support reaches J Camp, which uses wheelchair basketball to help girls with and without disabilities take part in sport.A report published by Play Academy on October 11, 2025, described how J Camp adapts its sessions with soft balls, hoops at different heights and a tambourine beneath a basket. These changes allow participants to try shots at their own pace. They can also choose their equipment and suggest changes to the rules.Makiko Harada, J Camp’s programme manager, explained the reason behind this approach in the October 11 report.“Children with disabilities often spend their days being helped, or holding back,” Harada said. “Here, they choose, decide and try on their own. Those small steps build self-confidence and self-efficacy.”The sessions give girls opportunities to make decisions for themselves instead of simply following instructions. They can try harder shots, create rules and encourage other participants. This is the kind of experience Play Academy aims to support by helping local organisations make sport more accessible. How Naomi Osaka’s initiative is helping young women become leadersPlay Academy’s support for J Camp also extends beyond participation. Through Push for Future, J Camp trains young women, including those with disabilities, in areas such as safeguarding and working with children with disabilities. They then become programme leaders and help run sessions.One of them, Yume, first discovered wheelchair basketball through a J Camp staff member when she was in high school. She joined the leadership programme in 2024 because she wanted to help create more places where everyone could enjoy sport, regardless of disability.In the Play Academy report, Yume described how the role helped her become more comfortable speaking with children and their parents.“I was so nervous speaking in front of the kids at first. But little by little, I started to go up and talk to them and their parents, and I’ve become more proactive. I’ve gained confidence—even if it’s just a little,” she said.Her experience shows how the programme can help young women develop skills they can use beyond the court. Harada also noted that seeing women take leadership roles can encourage girls to imagine themselves doing the same.According to the report, some participants have already told J Camp they want to become programme leaders when they grow up. Some leaders have also taken what they learned into diversity initiatives in their workplaces and communities.J Camp expanded its efforts to include wheelchair rugby in 2025, giving participants another sporting option.In Osaka’s case, the project reflects the goal she set when she launched Play Academy: giving more girls the chance to discover what sport can offer them. Through its support for J Camp, the initiative helps create opportunities not only for girls to play, but also for young women to become role models for others.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Neeraj Yadav death: Friend says she met para athlete hours before he was found beside SUV
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Neeraj Yadav, a 42-year-old three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist, was found dead beside his SUV near Maujpur metro station in northeast
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Neeraj Yadav, a 42-year-old three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist, was found dead beside his SUV near Maujpur metro station in northeast Delhi Monday night in a suspected case of suicide. Yadav, who hailed from UP, used to run Anshneer Sports Academy in Haryana’s Sonipat. He is survived by his wife and their three-year-old daughter.Police received information from GTB Hospital around 12.08 am Tuesday that a person had been brought to its emergency department and declared dead by the attending doctors.“A team reached Rajiv Gandhi Hospital, where the emergency services of GTB Hospital are currently being operated, and the body had already been shifted to GTB Hospital’s mortuary,” an officer said.During inquiry, a woman who had brought Yadav to the hospital told police she had been friends with him since Dec 2025. According to her statement, she went to Sonipat on Oct 27 to meet Yadav and tell him she could no longer remain in touch with him. She told police Yadav later dropped her off at Maujpur in his SUV.Around 9pm, when the woman returned to the area near Gate No. 1 of Maujpur metro station to check on him, she found him lying on the road beside his vehicle and rushed him to hospital.Jafrabad police station has begun proceedings under BNSS Section 194, which deals with police inquiries and reports in cases of suicide and other unnatural deaths. “We have not found any suicide note or video,” an officer said.Speaking to reporters, a relative of Yadav said, “He had struggled, fought his way through difficulties and continued playing. It is difficult for me to believe that he could take the extreme step.”He also said he was unaware of the woman who had accompanied Yadav before his death and called for her role to be examined.Despite being diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, Yadav pursued his sporting ambitions, playing wheelchair tennis between 2005 and 2012 before switching to para-athletics. His breakthrough came at the 2015 Delhi State Athletics Meet, where he won gold medals in the shot put, javelin and discus events.Yadav announced himself on the international stage at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, winning gold in the men’s F55 javelin throw with an Asian-record effort of 29.84 metres. He subsequently clinched two gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games in 2023, winning the javelin and discus events to take his career tally to three Asian Para Games titles.However, his career was clouded by an anti-doping case. National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended him after an out-of-competition sample collected in Bengaluru in 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid. He sought DNA testing of his sample through the anti-doping disciplinary process. He was later banned for four years.India’s chief para-athletics coach S Satyanarayana suggested Yadav may have been under emotional distress after missing the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games because of his doping suspension. “Medals at the Asian Para Games can bring substantial govt cash awards. But his suspension had not ended, and he could not compete. It is possible this affected him deeply,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rinkside Recap: Avalanche redeemed with a 5-2 win over New Jersey on home ice
articles.summary: Parker Kelly scores the game winning goal and the Avs bounce back!
articles.body:
Denver, CO — The New Jersey Devils are among the NHL's hottest teams, both in success and headlines, after winning games and the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes. The Colorado Avalanche are a perennial powerhouse with superstar talent, but they've struggled with inconsistent performances and disappointing defeats lately. The Avs welcomed Nicolas Roy back to the lineup, finally deploying a relatively healthy forward group. How will he and the Avalanche fare against the Devils, who are on their second back-to-back?

We got a look at the new bottom-nine forward lines, with Kadri slotting back into the third-center role. Nic Roy's return as a second-line winger seems to have ended (at least for now) the experiment of Nazem Kadri on the wing. With Roy's return, we also saw Fedor Svechkov slotted at 4C.

Both clubs got off the blocks slowly, with a combined two shots on net in the first five minutes. Colorado got the better of the two shots, with Jake Allen turning away Lehkonen on the doorstep after a slow-developing play from MacKinnon and Necas ended with a chance.

The Avalanche got their first power play of the night 11 minutes in when Brett Pesce hooked Logan O'Connor. Unfortunately for the Avalanche, they once again allowed a short-handed tally instead of capitalizing on the extra man. Connor Brown made it 1-0 for the Devils at 12:21 in the first period.

The healthy Avalanche took a hit later in the first frame, with Josh Manson struggling to get off the ice before heading straight down the tunnel with a noticeable limp. He did not return to the bench for the second period.

The first ten minutes of the second frame played out like a game between a team on the second of a back-to-back and a struggling group.

The second half of the middle frame was a bit more exciting, with the Avalanche earning and cashing in on a power play this time. Gabe Landeskog scored on a back-door play from Jaden Schwartz at 10:58 to restore the tie. Landeskog's goal marks his fifth of the season, putting him on pace for 32 goals.

The Devils earned two power plays late in the second period, setting up a 5-on-3 for the final 30 seconds, but the Avalanche survived.

The third period started with one second left on O'Connor's penalty and 1:28 on Brent Burns' penalty, so New Jersey got the briefest 5-on-3 before returning to a one-man advantage. The Avs would inevitably kill it off.

It didn't take long for Nazem Kadri to get the Avalanche on the board again after a beautiful net-front pass from Nicolas Roy found his stick. Kadri had no doubt, with time, space, and an open net. The Avalanche led 2-1 at 2:45 in the third.

Next, Parker Kelly got in on the depth scoring. Both goals two and three came off of assists for Brent Burns, but this one was all Parker. He broke in with Logan O'Connor, looked for him, but ultimately decided to fire one on. It beat Allen cleanly, giving Colorado the 3-1 lead at 3:47.

Colorado really started to take over, as Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz scored 3o seconds apart. MacKinnon's came on a patented MacKinnon speed play, and Schwartz scored after Sam Malinski's shot created a juicy rebound. The Avs led 5-1 at 12:30 in the third.

Connor Brown got his second of the night in the throwaway portion of the third, making it 5-1 for the Avalanche, and that's how it ended.

I told head coach Jared Bednar that Artturi Lehkonen can be heard communicating on the PK from the press box, and I asked how important that is to killing penalties. "I think it's important in every aspect of the game. The more vocal you can be, the better off you are gonna be. Communication eliminates confusion." Adding this regarding Lehkonen: "Lehky's pretty steady with it cause he's an intelligent guy and he knows it helps."

Gabe Landeskog said Cale Makar looked up the all-time hits leaders in Avalanche history and shared that information with Gabe and the rest of the group. Landeskog said, "I thought we did a good job of sticking with it; we were hungry, we were on pucks… we wanted to make sure we just bounced back," when asked about the Avalanche's response.

Nazem Kadri also spoke with the media after the game and said, "I was definitely yelling for it for sure," when asked if Nic Roy saw him on his tie-breaking goal in the third, and added, "That was a great play by him."

Parker Kelly had some interesting words about the penalty called on Logan O'Connor, which seemed like a relatively soft cross-checking minor. "Just unfortunate for sure kinda takes the wind out of your sails cause I felt like we were hummin'… then two calls that are just like 'what?'… like I said it's a tough job, and they're doing the best they can out there."

It's hard not to be negative about a top power-play unit that gives up more goals than it scores on a given night. Short-handed goals against have been a theme since last season, with the Avalanche leading the way in 2025-26. This hot-button issue won't go away if the Avalanche top unit can't start filling the net.

It's good to see the Avalanche bounce back and "return the favor," as Parker Kelly put it post-game; this time, New Jersey was on the second of a back-to-back, and Colorado brought home the win.

Nic Roy's return was noticeable almost immediately, starting with his assist on the Kadri goal. It was nice to see the forward group settle a bit with Kadri back at center.

The Calgary Flames come to town for another quick-turnaround rematch on Saturday at Ball Arena!

articles.title: Coachella falls 5-1 against Tucson
articles.summary: Ben McCartney scored two goals in the 5-1 win for Tucson.
articles.body:
PALM DESERT, Calif. — Behind Ben McCartney's two goals, the Tucson Roadrunners picked up a decisive 5-1 win over the Coachella Valley Firebirds.

Tucson improved to 5-2 on the season, while Coachella Valley fell to 3-4. Tucson's five wins are the second most in the Pacific Division.

"I'm not getting into it. I'm keeping that to myself," Coachella Valley head coach Derek Laxdal said when asked what isn't working with the group. "There wasn't much. There hasn't been much good lately. You can talk about guys being in and out of the lineup, but that's an opportunity for others to step up. We got some kids that are making the same mistakes night in and night out."

Coachella Valley has lost back-to-back games and fell to a game under .500 on the year.

The first period saw no scoring until the final 30 seconds, when McCartney scored his third goal of the season. Cameron Hebig was credited with the assist, his first of the season.

The Roadrunners took full control of the game in the second period, scoring three of their five goals. Just two minutes in,Tij Iginla scored his first goal of the season. Joshua Roy and Montana Onyebuchi each were credited with an assist.

The score became 3-0 when Austin Poganski scored his second goal of the season. Poganski's shot hit the top of the net and crossed the goal line at the halfway point of the period. Zac Jones notched his fourth assist of the season, and Caleb Desnoyers added his third.

Jones capped off a three-goal period for the Roadrunners at the 14-minute mark, assisted by Robbie Russo and Brandon Tanev. Jones' goal silenced the crowd at Acrisure Arena.

Penalties were a deciding factor against Coachella Valley in the second period, with 19 combined penalty minutes. Nathan Villeneuve was hit with a 10-minute game misconduct penalty after fighting prior to a puck drop.

The second period ended with Tucson holding 24 shots on target, 10 more than Coachella Valley.

It took just 23 seconds into the third period for the Firebirds to score their lone goal. Jagger Firkus scored his third goal of the season with assists from Kaden Hammell and Gustav Olofsson.

Five minutes later, Tucson answered when McCartney scored his second goal of the game. Poganski and Hebig were credited with the assists.

Coachella Valley continues its homestand Friday when it hosts the Henderson Silver Knights. Puck drop is scheduled for 7 p.m. at Acrisure Arena.

articles.title: ‘Not Going To Call Him Soft’ — Dan Le Batard ‘Super Surprised’ by Pat McAfee’s Outrage Over Not Being ‘Universally Liked’
articles.summary: Pat McAfee has built a sports-media empire by being loud, irreverent, and impossible to ignore. But after a University of Utah video mocked his on-air person...
articles.body:
Pat McAfee has built a sports-media empire by being loud, irreverent, and impossible to ignore. But after a University of Utah video mocked his on-air persona, the ESPN personality found himself on the receiving end of the criticism he routinely dishes out.

Former ESPN host Dan Le Batard is struggling to understand why McAfee appears to be taking it so personally, especially while McAfee is operating from one of the biggest platforms of his career.

Dan Le Batard Questions Pat McAfee's Expectations

Discussing McAfee's comments about Utah, Le Batard wondered whether the "College GameDay" personality had expected his larger-than-life personality to win over virtually everyone.

"I really do think that Pat McAfee thought he was going to do some of these things and just be universally liked," Le Batard said .

He approached the controversy through McAfee's familiarity with professional wrestling, where provoking a reaction is part of the spectacle. In Le Batard's view, McAfee has built a successful career by embracing that polarizing persona, but now appears uncomfortable when the reaction turned negative.

"I don't know if Pat McAfee is enjoying as much of this experience as I feel like most of us think that he should be given that he's on top of the world," Le Batard said.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

He also acknowledged how easily criticism can overshadow praise. His description of nine positive comments getting drowned out by one negative response framed McAfee's reaction as something recognizably human.

Still, the intensity of that reaction caught him off guard.

"I've just been super surprised. I'm not going to call him soft. A lot of people are doing that now. I'm not going to do that," Le Batard said.

Le Batard argued that having both passionate supporters and critics can be a valuable part of being a prominent media personality. He questioned why McAfee seemed so uncomfortable with occupying that space.

"The best thing you can be is have people on both sides feel passionately some kind of way so that everybody's in the tent," he said.

Utah Controversy Prompts a Broader Debate About McAfee

McAfee's complaints followed a video posted by Utah's official Instagram account featuring students mocking him before Saturday's "GameDay" broadcast.

Explaining his frustration Monday, McAfee emphasized that the university itself had distributed the video before he appeared in front of its crowd. He said criticism on students' own accounts would have felt different.

"I was just very, very uncomfortable," McAfee said.

Utah subsequently apologized, accepted responsibility for publishing the post, and said McAfee and the show remained welcome. ESPN also supported its host's safety concerns and emphasized its responsibility to protect the people working on the broadcast.

Le Batard's suggestion was that McAfee could find some freedom in accepting that a loud, opinionated entertainer will draw loud, opinionated responses.

articles.title: Blackhawks Already Looking For Specific Need in Trade Market
articles.summary: With a vastly underwhelming start to the 2026-27 regular season, the trade chatter has already begun surrounding the Chicago Blackhawks […]
articles.body:
With a vastly underwhelming start to the 2026-27 regular season, the trade chatter has already begun surrounding the Chicago Blackhawks before November has even arrived. That's never a promising sign.

Particularly when its the fifth year of general manager Kyle Davidson's rebuild, and everyone involved within the organization, the coaching staff, the players, and Davidson himself, had the expectation of at least competing for a Stanley Cup playoff spot this season.

So far through 12 games, the Blackhawks have only accrued eight points and have the second-worst points percentage in the entire league. They're 30th in goals against per game, 31st in goals per game and power-play percentage, and 32nd in 5v5 shot attempts per game and faceoff-win percentage. Basically, they're near the bottom in every major statistical category.

With much of the NHL roster now filled with Davidson's top draft choices since taking over in March 2022, including nine first or second-round picks, it's difficult not to be concerned. Sure, it's only 12 games, and the Blackhawks are among the youngest teams again this season, especially at center and defense. The schedule hasn't done them any favors, either.

But this was the year when the excuses had to stop, and the team needed to take a significant step in the rebuild, and they've failed to do so through the opening month. As a result, Davidson could already look to change things up with his roster via trade.

Before Tuesday's game against the Los Angeles Kings, in which the Blackhawks earned a much-needed 2-1 win to snap a three-game losing skid, Frank Seravalli joined Chicago Sports Network's pregame show and reported that Davidson has been active on the trade market recently.

According to Seravalli, Davidson is searching for shoot-first scoring wingers with size around the league.

Kyle Davidson has been actively looking for "shoot-first, scoring wingers with size." If the Blackhawks slide continues, "count on something bigger perhaps in the works." pic.twitter.com/zIOZngJ5aS — BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) October 27, 2026

Kyle Davidson has been actively looking for "shoot-first, scoring wingers with size." If the Blackhawks slide continues, "count on something bigger perhaps in the works." pic.twitter.com/zIOZngJ5aS

As Seravalli mentioned, the issue is every NHL club loves that specific player type, and quality ones don't become available very often. It's also still early enough in the season where most GMs aren't quite ready to part ways with top-tier talent. Davidson's inquiries have been unsuccessful thus far.

Regardless, Davidson has apparently now seen enough from his current squad to feel an adjustment must be made and is looking to bring in outside help. His willingness to engage in trade talks and do business has also seemingly made its way around the league.

As Bleacher Nation's Tab Bamford pointed out on Tuesday, 25 of 32 teams have had at least one front-office representative at the United Center for the Blackhawks past two games. There were 18 in attendance for Tuesday's game against Los Angeles, which is far more than usual.

Considering Seravalli's report on CHSN's pregame show that night, the timing doesn't seem coincidental.

I'll note that 25 of the 32 NHL clubs have been represented by at least one person on the United Center guest list between the last two #Blackhawks games (vs FLA & vs LAK) pic.twitter.com/w2lLSR3LDa — Tab Bamford (@The1Tab) October 27, 2026

I'll note that 25 of the 32 NHL clubs have been represented by at least one person on the United Center guest list between the last two #Blackhawks games (vs FLA & vs LAK) pic.twitter.com/w2lLSR3LDa

As far as who Davidson could look to bring in from another club, there's been plenty of speculation around Philadelphia Flyers' winger Owen Tippett recently. Tippett has only one goal through nine games this season and currently sits on injured reserve with an upper-body injury, but he's a proven goal scorer who's been part of trade rumors for quite some time now.

Tippett led the Flyers with 28 goals last year and has potted 20-plus in four straight seasons. He's also recorded over 220 shots on goal in three of the last four years and regularly plays with a shoot-first demeanor, something the Blackhawks are targeting and need more of in their forward group.

Another aspect of Tippett's game that should be attractive to Davidson is his willingness to be engaged physically, another area where the Blackhawks have been poor so far this season. The lack of physicality consistently shown from top to bottom on the roster has been jarring. Just six players have recorded double-digit hits, with rookies Roman Kantserov and Anton Frondell being the only two top-nine forwards with more than 10.

Tippett provides some bite along with his goal-scoring skills, leading all Flyers forwards with a career-high 166 hits last season. He's recorded at least 100 hits in each of the last four years. His addition would help the Blackhawks in multiple ways.

However, it's worth mentioning Tippett, 27, is entering the second year of an eight-year contract with a $6.2 million cap hit. The money is reasonable for his services, but having six more years under contract might not be appealing to Davidson. Tippett also has a ten-team no-trade clause in his contract, so who knows if he's even willing to accept a trade to Chicago.

Another potential option could be Pittsburgh Penguins' winger Rickard Rakell, who's scored at least 24 goals in three of the last four years. The Penguins are slowly transitioning to a younger squad amidst a sluggish start to the season, which could make Rakell available. He was listed at No. 7 on Chris Johnston's latest trade board for The Athletic .

Rakell, 33, is much older than Tippett and doesn't provide the same physicality, but has much less term on his current contract. Rakell has two years remaining with a $5 million cap hit. His deal carries an eight-team no-trade list.

The trade buzz between the Blackhawks and Flyers started on Saturday afternoon, when Anthony Di Marco from Daily Faceoff quoted Bamford's post on X suggesting Philadelphia could be interested in Frank Nazar .

Nazar — Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 24, 2026

Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 24, 2026

Since then, Di Marco has also reported the Flyers are perusing the trade market for a center, but are prioritizing those with top-six upside. In the article linked down below, Di Marco also wrote that Oliver Moore is another Blackhawks player they're interested in. Although, Philadelphia is apparently skiddish about Moore's long-term top-six potential and view Nazar much higher.

PHI is looking for a center but they are prioritizing ones with top-6 upside. It will likely cost them one of their wingers, and with Konecny having a NMC, is Tippett more likely the one ultimately traded? I explore that in my latest for @DailyFaceoff . — Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 27, 2026

Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 27, 2026

Considering both Nazar and Moore recently signed long-term extensions with the Blackhawks at very reasonable price tags for their upside, it seems somewhat unlikely that Davidson would be willing to part ways with either this early into the season and their respective careers. Never say never, though.

Nazar has been arguably the Blackhawks best forward so far this season, being the lone player on the team above 50 percent in expected goals and scoring chances at 5v5. He's created scoring opportunities at a better clip than anyone else on the team and has been terrific on the penalty kill. He's just struggled to finish.

With the way Nazar's performed this year, trading the 22-year-old would be a foolish decision at this point and would feel like addition by subtraction. Plus, Di Marco has since posted the Blackhawks "don't seem in the market to trade him right now".

I said the Flyers like him but also pointed out that "the Blackhawks don't seem in the market to trade him right now, DFO was told." — Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 28, 2026

I said the Flyers like him but also pointed out that "the Blackhawks don't seem in the market to trade him right now, DFO was told."

Anthony Di Marco (@ADiMarco25) October 28, 2026

Moore signed his new five-year extension only 34 days ago, so pulling the trigger on a trade involving him seems doubtful. While his two-way game has lacked consistency since becoming a full-time NHL player last season, the Blackhawks front office and coaching staff regularly rave about his work ethic and character. He's also Connor Bedard's closest friend on the team. The captain probably wouldn't be thrilled to see Moore traded.

The issue for the Blackhawks presumably wanting to keep those two forwards is they would net the greatest returns in the trade market at this point, in terms of players with a somewhat reasonable chance of getting dealt. Bedard and Frondell are obvious no-go's for other teams, and Kantserov should probably be in that category, too.

But outside of those three, who on the current roster could actually fetch a shoot-first scoring winger that can help swing the Blackhawks season back in the right direction? If another team is looking for an impact roster player in return, there are few attractive trade chips to come by in Chicago.

What the Blackhawks do possess are seven first-round draft picks in the next three NHL Drafts, and packaging some of those together might be Davidson's best shot to land what he's searching for. The AHL pipeline also has some intriguing young talent, including Nick Lardis, AJ Spellacy, Sacha Boisvert, and Marek Vanacker.

Davidson probably wouldn't love to trade any of those four forward prospects, but in order to get in this league, you have to give, and those are the most attractive minor-league trade chips in the Blackhawks' possession right now.

Former first-round pick Kevin Korchinski is another potential trade candidate, as he's played in just three of the Hawks first 12 games this season. The 22-year-old defenseman hasn't consistenty cracked the NHL lineup since his rookie year in 2023-24 but is no longer waivers-exempt, so playing in the AHL isn't an option this year. Korchinski was listed at No. 19 in Johnston's trade board 2.0 on Tuesday.

articles.title: USC defense gears up for Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State
articles.summary: The Trojans will welcome No. 2 Ohio State to town, tasked with trying to limit a Heisman frontrunner.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The USC defense has spent this week trying to fix something that won't show up on any stat sheet or box score: their trust. Several players who spoke after practice on Wednesday pointed to the same root issue from the Wisconsin loss. It wasn't talent or scheme, but a group that wasn't successful at picking each other up when things started going sideways.

Defensive tackle Alex VanSumeren said the fix isn't a new scheme or different approach, but a return to the same process the group has leaned on since January.

"That trust is built every single day," VanSumeren said. "We've been playing with each other so long...I know what this guy's going to do when I'm in with him. I know I can go to war with these guys."

Safety Prophet Brown agreed, framing last Saturday's defeat as a rare case where all three phases failed simultaneously, something he said seldom happens to a well-coached team.

"We all could have been better in our own right," he said. "I feel like at times, nobody necessarily picked each other up. We kind of just let it happen and didn't really step up for each other all the time."

Defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart didn't dress anything up, either, saying the locker room had hard, honest conversations this week. He described a defense that's "slowly getting back" to trusting the player next to it. He credited the group's constant grind since January for making those tough conversations possible in the first place.

Their progress will be tested in a significant way, with Ohio State's offense rolling into the Coliseum built around Heisman frontrunner wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Safety Prophet Brown didn't waste time pretending there's any real trick to slowing down Smith, the program's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Brown compared him to Rutgers' wideout KJ Duff, not as an equal, but as the closest reference point he's faced this season for a player defenses can't fully take away.

"They find a lot of different ways to get him the ball," Brown said. "So it's not about trying to completely eliminate him, but put a cap on him...he's a great player, and it's a great opportunity for us."

Smith, joined by the rest of the Ohio State receivers, will be playing their first full game with freshman quarterback Luke Fahey under center. The California native will, in all likelihood, be taking over starting duties from Julian Sayin, who suffered a season-ending injury to his throwing arm during a 19-15 victory over Indiana on Oct. 17.

VanSumeren added that he thinks USC's run defense has quietly improved from a season ago even if it doesn't always show up on highlight reels.

"I believe it has stepped up really good," he said. "A lot of that stuff is not seen...[it] doesn't pop off the screen. It's something that you see if you really watch the tape and you really dig into it."

Stewart agreed, pointing to Ohio State's supporting cast around Smith as the reason the group can't afford to fixate on one single matchup. He also didn't shy away from the extra motivation of facing a team with former friends and teammates on the other sideline, several of whom he said already know what kind of game it's going to be.

"They know it's going to be a long game for them," Stewart said. "It's going to be a great game. I'm just happy we get to fall back on our training, our trust, and as a team we're gonna show what we got this Saturday."

For a defense that insists its issues were never about ability, Saturday offers a clean gut check. There are no excuses to hide behind, and the best receiver in the country will be standing on the other side of the ball to test whether USC's trust has truly been built back up.

articles.title: Luka Doncic-less Lakers get back on track with win over Clippers
articles.summary: JJ Redick has foreshadowed a night like Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
JJ Redick has foreshadowed a night like Wednesday evening.

When the Lakers would need to play or rely on players they normally don't, for whatever the circumstances it may be for that given game.

And against the Clippers, which was the second night of the back-to-back set after Tuesday's home loss to the Trail Blazers , the circumstances were being without superstar guard Luka Doncic (back tightness) and Ziaire Williams (left foot soreness).

Despite being without their best player and one of their starting wings, the Lakers got back on track after their first loss of the season, beating the Clippers 103-85.

With Doncic sidelined, a significant amount of attention turned to Austin Reaves, the Laker's second-best player who has gotten off to a career-best start to the season.

The sixth-year guard has shown several times what he's capable of doing when he's the lone star in the lineup, recording box score numbers that rival All-NBA guards.

Clippers coach Ty Lue acknowledged the threat Reaves poses.

"He can beat you by himself. … He's elite," Lue said.

And the Clippers treated Reaves as such, using aggressive defensive coverages to disrupt a rhythm that's been challenging for opponents to slow down since the start of the season.

Reaves finished with 16 points on 6-of-16 shooting to go with eight turnovers, ending his streak of 23-plus-point games while shooting at least 54% from the field in four games.

But the Lakers didn't need a nuclear performance from Reaves.

They got Collin Sexton showing off why he's nicknamed the "Young Bull", with the veteran guard providing the "insanity", as Redick put it, on both ends of the floor that the team has come to celebrate.

They got Quentin Grimes, who stepped into the starting lineup for the first time, having his best two-way performance.

And they got a near perfect shooting night from Matisse Thybulle .

Sexton finished with 21 points, scoring nine straight points late in the third quarter that pushed the Lakers' lead from 13 to 20 points.

Grimes had a season-high 23 points to go along with five assists and four steals.

Thybulle scored 15 points on 5-of-6 shooting (4 of 6 on 3-pointers).

Veteran forward Jarred Vanderbilt made his season debut in light of the team's injuries, finishing with an individual plus/minus of plus-22 in 21 minutes.

The Clippers were short-handed, as they have been for most of the season, without Rui Hachimura , Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal.
