articles.title: Gonzaga’s Final Exhibition Ends in 91-59 Rout Over Lewis-Clark State
articles.summary: Consider making a donation to the Innovia Foundation in support of the Spokane wildfire relief efforts.
articles.body:
Sometimes life's unfortunate circumstances are much bigger than basketball. This charity exhibition with NAIA's Lewis-Clark State Warriors from Lewiston, Idaho, came together through the help of the Innovia Foundation and Spokane Region Long Term Recovery Group to help Spokane wildfire victims.

For Gonzaga Bulldogs coach Mark Few, along with the help of the Lewis-Clark State coaching staff, to put this together shows how much basketball in the Pacific Northwest can unite two schools and communities from the neighboring states of Washington and Idaho.

Few had this to say postgame about the experience:

"As time goes on, the support starts waning and dissipating. I wanted to make another statement that there is still need out there right now. These are people who watch us on TV every game, come to watch us play and are wanting to meet us. It's important that we stepped up."

As for the college basketball action inside the McCarthey Athletic Center, sophomore wing Davis Fogle made his return to the Gonzaga starting lineup after the 76-72 exhibition loss to the Arkansas Razorbacks back on Oct. 24. Fogle was sidelined with a left leg injury in Fayetteville, Arkansas.

The starting lineup from this matchup is what should be expected going forward: Fifth-year point guard Xaivian Lee, sophomore shooting guard Isiah Harwell, Fogle, redshirt senior power forward Braden Huff, and sophomore center Massamba Diop. Fifth-year forward Chauncey Wiggins is still ineligible for the Zags and was in street clothes on the bench.

Wiggins, a Florida State Seminoles transfer, is now attempting to join the 5-in-5 lawsuit in Waco, Texas, after withdrawing from the state of Georgia case before the game. The Spokesman-Review's Theo Lawson reports that the court hearing in Texas will take place starting on the morning of Oct. 29.

With an exhibition like this, it's hard to really pinpoint takeaways that will truly translate into Gonzaga's upcoming first true test. Here are a somewhat noticeable handful against a Lewis-Clark State group that is just excited to experience what the Kennel has to offer:

The program has been lacking rim protection for what seems like quite a long time now. Diop, the 7-1 Arizona State Sun Devils transfer, is going to bring a whole lot of that and more defensive upside to the table. It's about being in control of himself and not letting his emotions get the best of him, something that now Golden State Warriors forward Graham Ike dealt with early on in his tenure after transferring in from the Wyoming Cowboys.

The frontcourt depth speaks volumes with redshirt freshman forward/center Parker Jefferson's second-half outing off the bench. He ended up with 12 points on 6-of-9 field goals, six rebounds, two assists, and two blocks. While Jefferson may not see the floor much throughout the key stretches of the difficult non-conference slate, it's nice to know that he's readily available in Few's back pocket. The 6-9 native of Waxahachie, Texas, does the dirty work, simply fighting for his chance to receive meaningful minutes. Much respect to his dedicated workmanship, something that was instilled in him during his senior high school season in Inglewood, California.

Once the backcourt combination of fifth-year combo guard Javon Bennett and French combo guard Nathan De Sousa can get fully acclimated, that's a disruptive bench duo. It all depends on their consistency from beyond the arc and hitting at a high clip against top competition, something that hasn't been seen through the first two October scrimmages.

My overexaggerated take of the night? Spanish forward/center Izan Almansa is already one of the most underrated stretch bigs in the NCAA. The professional basketball background is going to pay off early and handsomely. Pretty hard to believe that the 21-year-old reportedly has three years of college basketball eligibility after spending three different seasons with the NBA G League Ignite, NBL's Perth Wildcats in Australia, and Real Madrid in the EuroLeague from 2023-26.

6-10 Almansa finished with a near-perfect shooting display off the bench against Lewis-Clark State: a tied-for-game-high 12 points on 4-of-5 field goals, 2-for-2 on catch-and-shoot three-point opportunities.

This KHQ/SWX broadcast could very well be the last with play-by-play Greg Heister and color commentator Dan Dickau together. Analyst Richard Fox wasn't present. While that trio was far from my favorite to listen to, I don't want to attack these Liliac City icons. They each deserve their own individual praise after being a part of a countless number of noteworthy memories during their careers working for the local television station.

No. 15-ranked Gonzaga's 2026-27 season opener comes against the Purdue Boilermakers at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada, on Nov. 2 at 4:30 p.m. PT on TNT. Coach Matt Painter's unranked group did receive 50 votes in the preseason AP Poll.

Similar to how Few's unit shot horrendously from deep against Arkansas (6-for-28, 21.4 percent), Purdue did the same in their 76-53 exhibition loss at the UConn Huskies in Hartford, Connecticut, back on Oct. 27 (2-for-25, 8.0 percent). That's for those who like to overreact to October encounters that don't matter.

More eeriness to leave you with heading into the Halloween weekend. The Zags have won 22 straight season openers, but are 0-5 all-time against the Boilermakers. What gives at the start of next week?

Arden Cravalho is a Gonzaga University graduate from the Bay Area… Follow him on X @a_cravalho

articles.title: Meet Makinley Cooper-Johnson, the Welsh darts-playing teenager hoping to beat Luke Littler
articles.summary: Makinley Cooper-Johnson is aiming to bury Luke Littler on the darts stage and use the prize money to become an undertaker.
articles.body:
A Welsh teenager will be aiming to bury Luke Littler on Friday evening – and use the six-figure prize money to become an undertaker.

It is an unusual goal to have in mind as you prepare to step on to the oche to face the reigning world champion.

But then it is not the norm to see a 14-year-old who only took up darts three years ago given a chance to topple the sport's leading light.

Makinley Cooper-Johnson is one of the 24 contestants chosen by Netflix to take part in the streaming giant's Beat Luke Littler broadcast.

A prize of £501,000 is on offer for the first to win a single leg of 501 against the world number one.

'Mighty Mak' is the second youngest to make it past the auditions after impressing the panel of judges, which included darts legend Phil Taylor.

After tips from the man they call 'The Power', the Wrexham rookie is not shy about his chances either.

"Look, I'm not saying I'm world class or anything, but I can hold my own," Cooper-Johnson told BBC Wales. "I've got a shot at this.

"I respect Luke for what he's done. But at the end of the day, he knows he's good – but he doesn't know how good I am."

If he throws as well as he speaks, the affable youngster may well have a chance at scooping the life-changing sum.

Promising to buy his brother a car is first on the agenda, and then setting up his own firm.

"Undertakers never go out of business, do they?" he said with a smile. "Money's money!

"Being successful is all I've ever wanted. Darts would be an amazing way to go for that, and I'd love to put some respect into the sport and hopefully achieve a lot.

"But I also love to entertain, whether that's on a darts stage or a programme."

A Freddie Mercury impression is part of his routine, and there were certainly no signs of being under pressure as hype around the programme builds, with Cooper-Johnson saying he almost didn't hang around to audition.

"It was uproar when we got there," he said, mum Stacie adding that the family only found out about his 'joke' application after receiving an invitation to the try-out.

"The queues were miles and miles of eager men and women all wanting to challenge one person, which is crazy to think about.

"I'd had enough of standing around and was walking back to the car before a steward in a high-vis showed me the queues for under-18s.

"It was still two hours in the rain, but we finally got in, and that's where it all kicked off."

And it ended with telephone tips from Taylor.

"My best mate Phil! I was in bed half-asleep when Mum came in with the phone," Cooper-Johnson said.

"When I heard who it was, I was out of bed, stood up, almost saluting, and he personally told me I had a place in the live show."

There is every chance judges were impressed with his ad-libs as much as his accuracy.

Cooper-Johnson says he is yet to hit a nine-darter, quipping "that treble 19 messes with me, man", but he has come a long way since starting three years ago.

He initially picked up darts to join his brother and father in the living room, "lobbing darts at an unusual board on an uneven wall…it was shocking!"

Mum Stacie, whose own interest in watching darts was reignited by Littler's emergence, added: "We know how much Makinley loves playing and we've noticed he's got better and better over the past six months.

"It's been a bit of a whirlwind since the audition, but the family are ecstatic and so proud of him."

They will be in the crowd at the Manchester Central Convention Complex as he aims to beat Littler, with Cooper-Johnson hoping his walk-out song suggestions get the green light – and that he gets an early crack at the champ.

"I don't know the order, but if I had to pick, Luke doesn't like playing earlier on," he said.

"He likes to settle into his game, so I'd probably like to be in there relatively shortly.

"But then again, you gotta give the fans a show, haven't you!"

Cooper-Johnson is one of three Welsh contestants on the show hoping to make a name for themselves.

Tony Cole, 39, from south Wales – known as 'Top Cat' – is a bank business adviser, while Pwyll ap Llyr Edwards from Llanuwchllyn is usually found putting up fences rather than aiming arrows.

Edwards has been playing since eight and also keeps bees, as well as playing the sport he has loved since early childhood.

"I started chucking a few darts when I was about three years old, then I started properly when I was about eight," he told BBC Radio Cymru.

"If I find my A game on the day and he doesn't, I might have a chance. It's going to be a big ask.

"I have had a few 12-darters and one or two 11-darters.

"But I will have to start the leg. If that happens, if I get a 12-darter, he has to get a nine-darter. But that's one of my best legs, so crossed fingers."

articles.title: ‘We miss him’ — Tom Bischof looking forward to seeing Vincent Kompany back at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: FC Bayern will have Vincent Kompany take his time to recover.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich have continued to get the job done despite Vincent Kompany's absence, with Aaron Danks stepping up to lead the team during the head coach's recovery. But while the results have remained positive, Tom Bischof admitted that something is inevitably different without the Belgian on the touchline.

Asked whether things might be a little quieter in the dressing room without Kompany, Bischof praised Danks while acknowledging just how much the team misses their head coach.

"I think Danksy is doing a good job too, and has a loud voice. He motivates us well, too, but of course, it's a bit different when Vinnie is standing in front of us. We miss him, but we're also happy that he's doing much better now and is back home. We're happy for him," Bischof said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

It is a nice insight into the atmosphere inside the Bayern dressing room. Danks has earned plenty of credit for keeping things moving, guiding Bayern to a 6-1 DFB-Pokal victory over FC Magdeburg, but Kompany's presence clearly means a great deal to the players.

The most encouraging news is that Kompany has been discharged from the hospital and is continuing his recovery at home with his family. There is still no set timeline for his return, and Bayern are rightly allowing him all the time he needs.

The players miss their coach, but his health comes first. Hopefully, it will not be too long before Kompany is back where he belongs — on the sidelines, leading Bayern Munich.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund’s Niko Kovač hoping for a speedy recovery for Vincent Kompany
articles.summary: Kovac wished Kompany a speedy recovery ahead of Dortmund’s win over Frankfurt
articles.body:
There's been an outpouring of well wishes for Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany after he collapsed last Friday at Säbener Straße following Bayern's first-team training session. The Belgian had just been getting over an infection as well as hip problems that had affected his ability to traverse the touchlines during Bayern's last two matches, but it's still unclear whether the collapse was related to the illness he was recovering from.

Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovač, who previously managed and played for Bayern, offered his own well wishes for his rival manager ahead of Dortmund's 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt that provisionally took them to the top of the Bundesliga table.

"Like all football fans, I wish him all the best. I hope he makes a speedy recovery and returns to the pitch as soon as possible. The most important thing at this stage is to give him some calm and quiet, because he needs time. We all know how demanding a coach's job is, so I genuinely wish him all the very best. I hope we'll be able to speak again at some point next week," the Croatian manager gracefully said (via @iMiaSanMia ).

Kovač is no stranger to the constant limelight and microscope Kompany is under as Bayern manager, and some reports have suggested that late nights, long days, and a relentless workload might have contributed to Kompany collapsing on Friday in addition to the illness he had been getting over. As the Croatian alluded to, Kompany will now be getting some proper rest as he recovers from what is always a concerning medical event, and he could wind up missing out on the season's second installment of der Klassiker against Dortmund at the end of the month. That match will likely have big implications in the title race for the first time in quite a few seasons with the way things have gone so far.

articles.title: Steph Curry proves he’s still got it matching stunning LeBron James stat in Warriors’ win
articles.summary: At 38 years old, Steph Curry is still doing things on the basketball court nobody else can.
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS — At 38 years old, Steph Curry is still doing things on the basketball court nobody else can. The umpteenth example: A 17-point flurry in the span of six minutes, the highlight being a heat-check 31-footer that, of course, found the bottom of the net.

Curry finished with 44, and the Warriors needed every last one of them to hold off the Timberwolves, despite Golden State pulling ahead by 24 after halftime and Minnesota playing its first game since Anthony Edwards learned he would require knee surgery.

With his first 40-piece of the season, Curry joined LeBron James in exclusive company. It was his 15th 40-point game since turning 35, tying James for the most in NBA history.

"I just see him doing what Steph Curry does," coach Steve Kerr said after the 119-114 win. "I've been watching him for so long that it never surprises me when he gets hot. What makes him special is it can happen at any time."

After starting 2-of-8 from the field Wednesday, Curry pulled up and connected on his first 3-pointer about three minutes into the second quarter. He drained another on Golden State's next possession and shouted at the Warriors' bench, who loved it.

Curry went on to connect on six of his next eight shots, pouring in 19 as the Warriors built a 64-48 halftime lead.

Despite building a lead that widened as far as 78-54 midway through the third quarter, the Warriors needed even more from Curry to close out a Minnesota team without its best player.

Sixteen of Curry's points came from the foul line, including an even dozen as he helped keep Minnesota at bay in the second half. It was Curry's second-highest total ever on foul shots.

He had gotten to the line 16 times three other times in his career, but the win over Minnesota — in career game No. 1,073 — was the first time he converted every single one of them.

"They were pressuring pretty much all the way out to half court, so you're gonna have those driving lanes," Curry said. "Thankfully it helped us in a couple lulls that we had, getting to the line, getting easy buckets, which we needed all of them."

Notably, Curry is also still doing things on the basketball court that would never be expected of a star of his caliber playing only the fifth game of his 18th season, especially not one coming off a season where injuries limited him to the third-fewest games of his career.

But that's exactly what Curry did, diving after a loose ball early in the second half. LaMello Ball went diving across the floor as Curry came away with possession — and narrowly avoided Ball barrelling into his lower half. Curry said he wasn't even thinking about his gimpy knee.

"I think that's just more indicative of how good I feel, considering the age and miles and how last year went that I even tried it, I had a confidence that I could get down there," Curry said. "There's situations where you find yourself in where you're just playing basketball and reacting, and that's one of those."

Curry had already secured his 40-point night when he checked out with the Warriors leading 100-87 with a little more than 9 minutes left to play. He was still at 26 minutes, and Kerr surely would have loved to allow him to rest for the remainder of the game.

Curry has been strictly capped at 32 minutes as the Warriors attempt to manage his ramp-up and keep the knee that cost him 27 games last season as healthy as possible.

He ended up coming 25 seconds shy of the limit imposed by the Warriors training staff but reached another milestone in the process — his first 30-minute night of the season.

"I honestly didn't know until after the game, which was nice that we were just kind of in the moment, playing," Curry said. "A little different flow to it when I got hot in the second, had to play a little bit of a longer stretch. So it's nice to keep building and feel good coming out of it."

articles.title: The Brewers were already great. Now, they’re undeniable
articles.summary: It was a long time coming but the Milwaukee Brewers now have the World Series championship their franchise has so richly deserved.
articles.body: When he walked off the mound, looking bothered but also somewhat bemused about a cramp that cut short his second World Series start, Jacob Misiorowski was treated to a standing ovation in two different stadiums. In Tampa, where he left after five-and-two-thirds scoreless innings, Brewers fans had invaded the opposing ballpark so thoroughly and loudly that the team might as well have been wearing white and batting second. Back in Milwaukee, watch parties at the team’s home ballpark sold out in minutes, with the $15 tickets re-selling for close to $300. The smallest media market in Major League Baseball made itself heard and seen and known en route to celebrating their first World Series championship. Brewers fans might have been the only ones who saw it coming. Shame on the rest of us. We call it the World Series, so perhaps it’s no wonder that the winner is often treated like a referendum to be critiqued on a global scale and not a champion to be beloved by the city it represents. Sports fans say they want the conclusive catharsis of a clear champion, but in truth it often seems we want the controversy of something more ambiguous. The appeal of sports is their ostensibly level playing field; the intrigue is in the gritty texture that reality tends to reveal. Thank goodness, millions of neutral fans said when the Dodgers were eliminated – and then a lot of them tuned out. There would be no big bad villain whose success makes the sport seem stacked against your favorite team. No national crisis of competitive imbalance. No compelling argument for an economic overhaul of the entire industry. Just a deserving champion. The Milwaukee Brewers won what was, ultimately, a bit of a boring World Series in five games. They won it for themselves, each other, and a fanbase that has never seen a championship. The only drama stemmed from the other team managing a single victory in the face of such undeniable dominance. In every matchup during this postseason, the team with the better record prevailed. In the end, the team with the best record was left standing. The team with the highest collective batting average, the soon-to-be Cy Young Award winner, and the reigning two-time Manager of the Year turned out to be pretty great. They won fair and square and in spite of MLB’s payroll disparity. There is nothing left to debate. (In a baseball sense; a knock-down, drag-out labor battle still lies ahead.) A bunch of gamers When they toppled the Dodgers – who were presumed to be on path to a title three-peat from Opening Day all the way until they were swept – manager Pat Murphy called his guys gamers in juxtaposition to L.A.’s Hall of Famers. It was an instant classic of a quote, a brilliant bit of marketing, and a surprisingly accurate description of what the Brewers do well for something so reductionist. And yet, the implication – that the Brewers are categorically underdogs – was ultimately rendered moot by what they did next. Misiorowski set a World Series record for speed on the first pitch of Game 1. Aaron Ashby headlined a nearly bulletproof bullpen by setting a postseason record for consecutive scoreless innings. Twenty-two-year-old rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt had a record-setting six-straight hits across the final two games of the Fall Classic. Jackson Chourio set a five-game World Series record with 11 hits. Somehow none of them were the World Series MVP. That honor was ultimately bestowed upon catcher William Contreras, who hit .381 in the series while receiving constant kudos from his pitching staff, for whom he stole an extra 10 strikes through successful Automated Ball-Strike System challenges. It was a World Series for true ball lovers – low on homers, resplendent with action and outs on the basepaths. There were game-saving catches and costly errors. It featured the two top seeds in the postseason and, even when the score was close, it didn’t really feel like the Tampa Bay Rays stood a chance. In the end, the Brewers went 11-2 in October. Against the best teams the 2026 season could throw at them, they looked completely in control. They haven’t lost consecutive games since Labor Day weekend, almost two months ago. Nearly a decade in the making If you just tuned in, this has been a long time coming. Now the captain, Christian Yelich arrived in Milwaukee via a trade from the Miami Marlins in January 2018. The Brewers had never won the World Series and had gone six years without making the postseason. That year, Yelich won the National League MVP; the Brewers won 96 games, the division, and came within one win of the pennant. It was the beginning of one of the quietest stretches of sustained success in recent history. From the start of 2018 through the end of the 2026 regular season, the Brewers won the fourth-most games in Major League Baseball. Before this month, though, it failed to translate to October. They made the playoffs in seven of the last eight years. That whole time, they won 11 combined postseason games. Skeptics and – let’s be honest – probably some fans worried that this was the real problem with baseball’s Haves and Have Nots. Small markets might win on the margins of a six-month marathon; but you need stars to succeed under the bright lights of October. The analytic-minded architect who assembled so much underrated talent left for the biggest market in baseball. The manager who made them more than the sum of their parts left for their division rival to become the highest-paid skipper in the sport. Still, the Milwaukee Brewers won. Each of the past five seasons, more than the year before. On Opening Day, FanGraphs gave the Brewers, who had just won the most regular-season games in 2025, a 2.1% chance to win the World Series. Fourteen teams had better odds. They were perfectly, innocuously, middle-of-the-pack. They went on to win a franchise-record 103 games in the regular season. They won the necessary 11 more in the postseason handily. “It only took four months,” the rookie Pratt marveled, gobsmacked and goofy in the minutes following the final out. It was perfect for how ironic it was. A 22-year-old – who signed an eight-year, $50.75 million contract in April and debuted for the team in June – would say that. He arrived just in time to help the Brewers become an impossible-to-ignore force in the sport. It only took 57 years.

articles.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 on penalties to reach League Cup quarterfinals
articles.summary: After a 1-1 draw in normal time, Liverpool win 6-5 to edge a narrow win after penalties in last-16 match at Anfield.
articles.body:
Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 in a dramatic penalty shootout to reach the English League Cup quarterfinals.

In a clash between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso, it was the Liverpool manager who took the bragging rights in the last-16 tie at Anfield on Wednesday.

A 1-1 draw in normal time set the stage for the shootout as Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers netted from the spot, only for Cody Gakpo to equalise with a penalty of his own just before half-time.

Chelsea’s Valentin Barco hit the post in the shootout before Liverpool’s Kostas Tsimikas wasted a chance to win it when he blazed over.

Ryan Gravenberch was denied by Chelsea keeper Mike Penders, but Giorgi Mamardashvili saved Emmanuel Emegha’s kick to keep Liverpool alive.

After Joe Gomez scored for Liverpool, Blues defender Wesley Fofana miscued into the Kop as the hosts advanced.

It was former Liverpool midfielder Alonso’s third defeat in his three visits to Anfield as a manager, following losses with Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and Real Madrid in 2025.

In their debut campaigns at Liverpool, Jurgen Klopp and Arne Slot both reached the League Cup final, and Iraola is on course to follow in their footsteps with the 10-time winners of the competition.

“We are really happy. Three wins at home in a row is very important. We were struggling at home in the league but now we go against Arsenal on Sunday,” said Iraola, who will face his former club Bournemouth in the last eight.

Alonso added: “Every time you reach the penalties, someone will feel it is harsh to go out of the competition.

“We were showing a good level and this is what it takes to come to these stadiums. The Premier League is the main focus.”

Alonso made just four changes to the Chelsea side that lost 2-0 at home to Tottenham on Saturday, while Iraola made seven changes from Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday.

Rogers put Chelsea in front with a 40th-minute penalty after Gravenberch clattered into Moises Caicedo.

But Liverpool were level three minutes later with a penalty of their own as Gakpo converted from the spot following Fofana’s handball.

articles.title: Man City beat Brighton on penalties after dramatic League Cup comeback
articles.summary: Manchester City overcome Brighton 4-3 on penalties after 2-2 draw and will play Bradford for a spot in the semifinals.
articles.body:
Manchester City have avoided the fate that befell Arsenal by winning a penalty shootout against Brighton to advance to the quarterfinals of the English League Cup.

City stayed on course to retain the title by twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Brighton at home, then triumph 4-3 in the shootout.

Backup goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli saved Brighton’s last two spot kicks — from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk — to rescue City, which had fallen behind in the shootout when Mateo Kovacic had the team’s fourth penalty saved.

City boss Enzo Maresca made nine changes after Saturday’s loss at Aston Villa — which ended the leaders’ 100 percent start to the Premier League campaign.

Erling Haaland, Ruben Dias, Elliot Anderson and Gianluigi Donnarumma were among the City stars rested.

Brighton went in front after 30 minutes when Malick Yalcouye steered Georginio Rutter’s shot past Rulli from five yards.

Kovacic hauled City level 20 minutes later with a fine finish that curled into the far corner from 25 yards.

Rutter restored Brighton’s lead two minutes after half-time, slotting home from Jaouen Hadjam’s cut-back.

Vitor Reis deflected in Rayan Cherki’s 72nd-minute free kick to equalise for City.

Kovacic’s penalty was saved by Jason Steele in the shootout, but Rulli denied Brighton’s Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City into the last eight.

The sides meet again in the Premier League at the Etihad on Saturday.

City will meet third-tier Bradford for a place in the semifinals.

Bournemouth beat Aston Villa as run continues

Bournemouth extended their blistering run with a 3-0 win against Aston Villa at the Vitality Stadium.

The Cherries beat AC Milan 3-0 in the Europa League last week and followed that up with a 3-0 win at Manchester United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Crystal Palace eased the pressure on under-fire boss Pierre Sage with a 1-0 win at Fulham.

In the quarterfinals, Palace host Sunderland, who enjoyed a welcome respite from their Premier League struggles with a 3-2 victory against Brentford at the Stadium of Light.

Fourth-tier Fleetwood reached the quarterfinals with a stunning penalty shootout victory over Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday.

The “Cod Army” will face the winners of Thursday’s clash between Everton and Newcastle.

articles.title: Stephen Curry, Warriors hold nerve to beat Timberwolves in tight NBA battle
articles.summary: Warriors beat Timberwolves, Philadelphia 76ers power past Indiana Pacers and Cleveland Cavaliers top Washington Wizards.
articles.body:
Stephen Curry scored 44 points and grabbed eight rebounds, and the Golden State Warriors escaped with a 119-114 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves in Minneapolis.

Yaxel Lendeborg added 26 points in Wednesday night’s match for Golden State, which won its second straight game after losing its first three contests of the season. Brandon Williams chipped in 11 points off the bench.

Jonathan Kuminga scored 20 points against his former team to lead Minnesota, which dropped its second game in a row after a 3-0 start. Jaden McDaniels and Terrence Shannon Jr each finished with 19 points, and Ayo Dosunmu contributed 17.

The Timberwolves outscored the Warriors 66-55 in the second half but could not complete the comeback attempt. Bones Hyland made a bank shot to trim the deficit to three points in the final seconds, but Curry ended the scoring with two free throws.

The Warriors led 93-81 at the end of the third quarter.

Golden State increased its lead to as many as 24 points midway through the second half. Curry converted a three-point play to give the Warriors a 78-54 lead.

Minnesota closed the third quarter on a 27-15 run to cut the deficit to 12. Hyland came off the bench and made a pair of 3-pointers to help the Timberwolves draw closer.

The Warriors closed the first quarter on a 21-9 run to grab a 30-23 advantage. De’Anthony Melton knocked down a pair of 3-pointers during the run, and Lendeborg added a driving layup and a 3-pointer.

Another layup by Lendeborg gave Golden State its first double-digit lead of the game at 48-38 with 6:29 left in the half.

Golden State scored seven of the final nine points of the first half to go ahead by 16. Lendeborg made a 3-pointer and Will Richard and Curry made two free throws apiece.

Simons fuels fourth-quarter flurry as 76ers power past Pacers

Tyrese Maxey led a balanced attack with 27 points, and Anfernee Simons ignited a deficit-erasing, fourth-quarter run, as the Philadelphia 76ers overtook the Indiana Pacers for a 114-109 victory in Indianapolis.

Simons finished with 20 points off the bench, while Joel Embiid had 21 points and 11 rebounds, Jaylen Brown 20 points and 10 rebounds and LeBron James had 13 points and 10 assists for the 76ers.

Pascal Siakam totalled 26 points to complement 11 rebounds and Andrew Nembhard chipped in with an 18-point, 14-assist double-double for the Pacers.

In a game that featured a 37-point explosion by the 76ers in the second quarter and two Pacers bursts during a 36-point response in the third period, Philadelphia found itself down 88-75 before dominating the final 12 minutes.

Simons buried a 3-pointer 18 seconds into the fourth quarter and the 76ers didn’t slow down until they had run off 26 of the period’s first 34 points to go up 101-96 with 4:24 to go. He had another 3-pointer in the run, James added one and Embiid contributed a three-point play.

Consecutive hoops by Siakam and Nembhard got the hosts within one with 3:07 to play, and it remained a one-score game into the final 90 seconds until Maxey secured Philadelphia’s fourth win in five games with a pair of 3-pointers in the final 1:10.

The 76ers outscored the Pacers 39-21 in the final period.

Indiana had taken its second-half lead with 17-0 and 13-2 third-quarter flurries, the latter helping put the 76ers in a 13-point hole entering the final 12 minutes.

Aaron Nesmith had 18 points, Kelly Oubre Jr had 15 and Obi Toppin had 13 for the Pacers, who lost their second straight.

Cavaliers spoil AJ Dybantsa’s Wizards debut

Evan Mobley scored 24 points and Peyton Watson had a season-high 22 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the visiting Washington Wizards 121-111, spoiling the NBA debut of top overall draft pick AJ Dybantsa.

Dybantsa had a team-high 19 points in 27 minutes, making 8 of 12 field goal attempts with two rebounds and two assists.

Mobley, who scored 10 points in the fourth quarter, also grabbed 12 rebounds as Cleveland rallied from a 13-point deficit. Donovan Mitchell posted 19 points and seven assists, and Jarrett Allen had eight points, 12 rebounds and three blocks.

Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr each scored 18 points for the Wizards, while Kyshawn George had eight points and a career-high 11 assists. Trae Young added 14 points and eight assists, and Bilal Coulibaly made 8 of 9 shots and scored 17 off the bench.

The Cavaliers went in front for the first time since the first quarter at 94-92 on Mobley’s slam to begin the fourth. Dybantsa put Washington back ahead 105-104, but Cleveland scored the next nine points in completing a perfect three-game homestand.

Dybantsa drove the lane two minutes into the third to extend the Wizards’ lead to 76-63, but Cleveland ended the period on a 29-16 run. Mitchell made two free throws to tie it at 92-92 going into the fourth.

Coulibaly scored 14 points without a miss in the first half as Washington carried a 69-59 advantage into the break. Dybantsa had 11 points in 14 minutes and Young had seven points and six assists, while Watson had 16 for the Cavaliers.

Sarr scored 13 points in the first, his season high for a game, as the Wizards built a 42-34 lead. Dybantsa, Mitchell and Mobley all had nine points apiece as the teams combined to make 9 of 13 3-point attempts and go 15 of 16 at the foul line.

Dybantsa attacked the basket on the opening possession, drawing a foul and making two free throws 16 seconds in.

articles.title: Roberto Gómez relata el angustioso momento que vivió tras el accidente de tren: "Hubo un momento que me agobié"
articles.standfirst: El periodista explicó en La Tribu de Radio MARCA que recibió cientos de llamadas y mensajes después de que trascendiera que un Roberto Gómez viajaba en el tren accidentado.
articles.summary: El periodista explicó en La Tribu de Radio MARCA que recibió cientos de llamadas y mensajes después de que trascendiera que un Roberto Gómez viajaba en el tren accidentado.
articles.body: Roberto Gómez vivió ayer una jornada especialmente complicada. El periodista deportivo recibió cientos de llamadas y mensajes después de que trascendiera que una persona con su mismo nombre viajaba en el tren accidentado. Una situación que ha relatado este jueves en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, en una conversación con Raúl Varela marcada por la tristeza y la conmoción ante la tragedia. "Yo estaba precisamente con Vicente del Bosque y empezaron a llegar mensajes: '¿Cómo estás?, ¿dónde estás?, ¿cómo estás?'. Y yo no entendía absolutamente nada", explicó Roberto Gómez. El periodista comenzó entonces a recibir llamadas de diferentes medios de comunicación que querían conocer su situación. "Me llamaban de programas, me llamó de dos programas, de Onda Cero, de TV3, de Televisión Española, de todos los programas para entrar. Y la cantidad, los cientos, los cientos de llamadas", relató. La confusión provocó una avalancha de mensajes que terminó desbordando al periodista. "Tuve que contestar a los cientos, y repito, cientos. Hubo un momento que me agobié, lo reconozco, que me agobié", confesó. Roberto explicó que todo se debía a la coincidencia de su nombre con el de otro compañero: "Es que es un compañero, que se llama Roberto Gómez, y claro, de Onda Cero, yo que he estado en Onda Cero...". Más allá de lo ocurrido personalmente, Roberto Gómez quiso trasladar sus condolencias a las víctimas y sus familiares. "Qué tristeza, qué dolor y qué sensación tan dura, tan dura. Un accidente gravísimo, durísimo y con un impacto terrible", lamentó. También tuvo palabras de agradecimiento para los servicios de emergencia por su actuación y destacó la solidaridad mostrada durante las últimas horas. El periodista también reclamó explicaciones sobre lo sucedido. "Yo creo que hay que depurar responsabilidades, y cuanto antes, por supuesto, hay que hacerlo", aseguró, después de recordar la confianza que existía en la alta velocidad española. Finalmente, Roberto Gómez insistió en que el protagonismo debía estar en las víctimas y sus familias. "Hoy no toca. Hoy toca el estar muy pendiente de los heridos, de que se recuperen, dar el homenaje, como se merecen también, a los fallecidos, y, sobre todo, depurar responsabilidades", concluyó en La Tribu de Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Raúl Varela defiende a Marcos Llorente: "No tienen obligación, pero tampoco tienen prohibición de posicionarse"
articles.standfirst: El director de La Tribu aplaude que el futbolista del Atlético de Madrid se haya pronunciado públicamente tras la tragedia ferroviaria y defiende el derecho de los deportistas a expresar sus opiniones.
articles.summary: El director de La Tribu aplaude que el futbolista del Atlético de Madrid se haya pronunciado públicamente tras la tragedia ferroviaria y defiende el derecho de los deportistas a expresar sus opiniones.
articles.body: Las palabras de Marcos Llorente en redes sociales tras la tragedia ferroviaria han generado un intenso debate. El futbolista del Atlético de Madrid compartió un mensaje que fue difundido también por otros jugadores, entre ellos Carvajal, Courtois, Álex Baena y Marc Pubill. Una reacción que Raúl Varela ha querido respaldar durante su intervención en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, defendiendo el derecho de los deportistas a pronunciarse sobre cuestiones que van más allá del fútbol. "Mis dieces para Marcos Llorente. Para él y para todos los que de forma inmediata repostearon en sus redes sociales ese mensaje", ha comenzado señalando Varela, que ha relacionado la publicación con sus críticas a la gestión política de la seguridad ferroviaria. El periodista ha destacado que otros futbolistas se sumaron rápidamente a la difusión del mensaje, al igual que numerosos seguidores del jugador rojiblanco. Varela ha defendido que los futbolistas puedan expresar públicamente sus opiniones sin que su condición de deportistas suponga una limitación. "Los deportistas no tienen ninguna obligación de opinar sobre todos los temas de actualidad. No tienen obligación, pero tampoco tienen prohibición de posicionarse a favor o en contra de lo que sea", ha asegurado. El director de La Tribu también ha reivindicado el derecho de Llorente a exigir explicaciones a los responsables públicos. "Desde el respeto y la legalidad está absolutamente legitimado para exigir cuentas", ha afirmado, recordando que el jugador, como cualquier otro ciudadano, puede verse afectado por los problemas del transporte ferroviario. El periodista ha recordado que miles de personas utilizan diariamente las líneas de alta velocidad y que los propios futbolistas también son usuarios habituales de estos trenes. En este sentido, ha mencionado los desplazamientos de Llorente a Sevilla para disputar partidos en La Cartuja, el Sánchez-Pizjuán o el Benito Villamarín, insistiendo en que nadie está al margen de una tragedia de estas características. Por último, Varela ha respondido a quienes cuestionan que el futbolista se pronunciara inmediatamente después del accidente. "El problema para algunos [...] es que no se puede escribir en caliente y menos si eres una figura de notable relieve social", ha señalado. El director de La Tribu ha cerrado su reflexión reafirmando su defensa de la libertad de expresión de los deportistas: "Bienvenidos a una sociedad libre con ciudadanos libres como Marcos Llorente".

articles.title: "Si Llorente hubiese puesto lo contrario, ¿tendría el aplauso de los mismos o la crítica de los otros?"
articles.standfirst: Ricardo Rosety reflexiona sobre la polémica generada por las declaraciones del futbolista del Atlético de Madrid tras el accidente ferroviario de Toledo
articles.summary: Ricardo Rosety reflexiona sobre la polémica generada por las declaraciones del futbolista del Atlético de Madrid tras el accidente ferroviario de Toledo
articles.body: Paul Tenorio, Pedro Riesco, Ricardo Rosety, Pablo Pinto, Ferran Martíonez y Yon Cuezva han sido los tertulianos de este jueves en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por el accidente de tren de Toledo, la ronda de Copa y la llegada de Eder Sarabia al Espanyol. Raúl Varela ha defendido el derecho de Marcos Llorente a pronunciarse sobre lo sucedido, aunque ha dejado claro que no comparte ciertos comportamientos. "No comparto nada de las gafas amarillas, de lo que dice del Sol y de las gilipolleces que hace de andar descalzo con los perros a cinco grados bajo cero", ha señalado el presentador, matizando que se trata de su opinión personal. Sin embargo, ha respaldado su decisión de alzar la voz: "El hecho de que haya tenido la valentía de hablar, independientemente de que tendría que haberlo hecho a las diez de la mañana o a las diez de la noche, no creo que merezca el reproche por parte de nadie". Paul Tenorio ha compartido la reflexión de Varela y ha defendido que cualquier personaje público pueda pronunciarse sobre cuestiones ajenas a su profesión. "Yo creo que el deportista, el actor, el político, cuando se posiciona sobre algo que no es su sector, tienen todo el derecho del mundo a expresarse", ha explicado. Sin embargo, Tenorio también ha advertido de las consecuencias que pueden tener estas intervenciones. "Hay gente con mucha formación que entra a hablar en el terreno público y lo hace desde la sensatez, desde la reflexión, desde la serenidad, desde el conocimiento, y hay gente que emite exabruptos", ha afirmado. En cualquier caso, considera que "cada uno queda como quede en función de la calidad de la información, de su opinión, de la reflexión que haga". Sobre las palabras concretas de Marcos Llorente, el tertuliano ha sido contundente: "Creo que Llorente se ha limitado a manifestar un asunto que nos escama a todos, que es el político tuitero". Tenorio también ha señalado que los deportistas son conscientes de que posicionarse públicamente puede provocar la pérdida de seguidores, algo que, a su juicio, da valor a su decisión de pronunciarse. Por su parte, Ricardo Rosety ha llevado el debate hacia la capacidad de la sociedad para aceptar opiniones diferentes. "El problema no lo tienen los deportistas, actores, famosos o conocidos que opinan: el problema es nuestro como sociedad", ha asegurado. Rosety ha terminado planteando una reflexión sobre las reacciones que generan estas declaraciones: "¿Estamos preparados para escuchar algo que no compartimos? ¿Estamos preparados para que alguien meta su opinión tajante como Llorente, Guardiola o Piqué?". El periodista ha ido un paso más allá y ha puesto sobre la mesa una pregunta: "Si Marcos Llorente hubiese puesto lo contrario, ¿tendría el mismo aplauso de los mismos o la crítica de los otros?".

articles.title: Winners and Losers From the First Month of the 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: It's been a month since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 NHL regular season. As with the start of every season, it's brought its share of surprises and notable news.
articles.body:
It's been a month since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 NHL regular season. As with the start of every season, it's brought its share of surprises and notable news.

We've seen this era's greatest scorer on an early pace to set a single-season points record. A blockbuster trade on the eve of opening day, followed by another nearly a month later. We've also seen a promising young team serving notice that they're poised to challenge the top teams in the Western Conference.

The past four weeks also had their share of disappointments. Some rebuilding teams are struggling, as are some promising clubs coming off strong performances last season. It also wasn't a good month for a couple of veteran-laden teams.

Join us as we look back on the first month of this NHL campaign to determine its winners and losers.

Calling a rebuilding team a loser in the opening month of a season feels like kicking them when they're down. They're in the middle of an often difficult transition and they will be outplayed on most nights.

Nevertheless, there's no sugarcoating what the Vancouver Canucks and Chicago Blackhawks are currently enduring. They are the two worst teams in the NHL, and there's no indication they'll get any better as the season rolls along.

The Canucks' placement in the basement isn't unexpected. Their rebuild began when they traded superstar Quinn Hughes to Minnesota last December. That lead to further trades of several core veterans, along with the offseason changes in management and the coaching staff.

Chicago, however, shouldn't be in this situation following four years of rebuilding. However, they continue to disappoint despite a roster led by young superstar Connor Bedard and filled with promising talent like Frank Nazar, Anton Frondell, and Artyom Levshunov.

We would've included the Calgary Flames on this list after they lost six of their first seven games. However, they've since won four straight, including victories over the Minnesota Wild, Toronto Maple Leafs, and defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

Perhaps Vancouver and Chicago can draw inspiration from the Flames' recent red-hot streak and claw their way up the standings. However, it seems more likely that they'll still be near the bottom of the standings in a month's time.

Several clubs emerging from long rebuilds last season were expected to be among the early challengers for first place in their respective divisions.

However, the Anaheim Ducks, Buffalo Sabres, Montreal Canadiens, Philadelphia Flyers, and San Jose Sharks have endured their share of inconsistency throughout October, much to the disappointment of some of their fans.

On the other hand, the Utah Mammoth have thus far performed to expectations, jockeying with the Minnesota Wild for first place in the Central Division. Having made the playoffs last season, the Mammoth want to take the next step toward becoming a potential Stanley Cup contender.

Led by veteran scorers Clayton Keller and Nick Schmaltz, rising stars Dylan Guenther and Logan Cooley, and puck-moving defenseman Mikhail Sergachev, the Mammoth are among the league's highest-scoring teams . Their 3.62 goals-per-game average ranks sixth overall.

The Mammoth also made some notable offseason additions, signing free agent left winger Anders Lee and acquiring versatile forward Vincent Trocheck. Their experience and leadership have been invaluable during this season.

Defensive issues remain for the Mammoth. Their 3.31 goals-against per game is the league's 10th-highest, while their penalty-killing (67.4) ranks 29th. Nevertheless, their overall performance in October indicates they're on the right track as they attempt to establish themselves as a legitimate playoff contender.

According to James Mirtle of The Athletic, the average age of an NHL team in 2026-27 is 28.5. Eleven of those teams have an average age of 29 or older.

Most of those 11 clubs have had varying degrees of success during the opening month, sitting atop or near the top of their divisions. However, the Los Angeles Kings and Pittsburgh Penguins struggled as the month went on.

The Kings entered this season with the league's oldest roster (31.4), featuring greybeards Drew Doughty, Corey Perry, Mats Zuccarello, and Darcy Kuemper. The result is a club struggling to stay out of the Western Conference basement .

The Penguins (29.3) have spent the past two seasons transitioning from aging veterans to younger players. Having endured a 3-6-1 stretch between Oct. 7 and 24, management is reportedly willing to entertain offers for older stars like Erik Karlsson, Kris Letang, Rickard Rakell, and Bryan Rust.

It's possible the Kings and Penguins regain their footing and rise in the standings as the season progresses. However, their sputtering performances throughout the opening month suggest some of their veterans may no longer have what it takes to help their clubs as they once did.

Which Teams Are Pretenders or Contenders? 🤔

Winners: Fans of Early Season Blockbuster Trades

The imposition of the salary cap in 2005 all but ended the era of early-season blockbuster trades in the NHL.

Most clubs carried limited salary cap space to start the season because they used most of it during the offseason to bolster their rosters.

Before this season, blockbuster moves rarely occurred early in an NHL season, with some notable exceptions .

On Nov. 30, 2005, the Boston Bruins traded Joe Thornton to the San Jose Sharks. It was nearly 16 years before the next one happened, as the Buffalo Sabres shipped Jack Eichel to the Vegas Golden Knights on Nov. 4, 2021.

Since this season kicked off, however, we've had two blockbuster deals.

The first one occurred the day before opening night, but it generated plenty of buzz that carried over into the start of this season. On Sept. 28, the Columbus Blue Jackets and Toronto Maple Leafs made a six-player swap , with winger Kirill Marchenko heading to Toronto for power forward Matthew Knies.

Over three weeks later, the Winnipeg Jets shipped three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for forwards Dawson Mercer and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nico Daws, prospect center Alexander Command, and two draft picks.

Each trade happened for different reasons, but the common factor was that the teams involved had more salary-cap flexibility. The sharp rise of the cap from $95.5 million last season to $104 million left several clubs flush with cap dollars and a willingness to spend in the trade market.

The salary cap will rise to $113.5 million for 2027-28 and is projected to reach a whopping $127.5 million for 2028-29 . That means more October blockbusters in the offing over the next two years.

Losers: Promising Eastern Conference Teams

The Buffalo Sabres, Montréal Canadiens, and Philadelphia Flyers entered this season facing heightened expectations. The Sabres ended a league-record 14-season playoff drought by finishing atop the Atlantic Division. The Canadiens reached the Eastern Conference Final, and the Flyers reached the second round.

So far, however, the Sabres, Canadiens and Flyers have had disappointing opening-month performances.

The Sabres were inconsistent through the opening month (5-4-3). Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen's stats are among the worst for starting goaltenders. Young forwards Josh Doan, Konsta Helenius, and Jiri Kulich have struggled to score , and they've fallen behind early in too many games.

Injuries to key players like Nick Suzuki, Ivan Demidov, Mike Matheson, Kaiden Guhle, and Oliver Kapanen tested the Canadiens' depth. Undisciplined penalties, sloppy defensive play, and the inconsistency of starting goalie Jakub Dobeš contributed to a 4-3-2 record in their first nine contests .

The Flyers were dreadful through their first nine games (0-6-3). Their anemic 1.93 goals-per-game is the league's worst, as Tyson Foerster, Owen Tippett, and promising rookie Porter Martone struggled to score. Injuries to key players like Tippett, Travis Konecny and Rasmus Ristolainen didn't help.

As the opening month ends, the Canadiens have reeled off three straight wins, suggesting they could be overcoming their earlier woes. The Sabres still seek consistency, while the Flyers are struggling to claw their way out of the Eastern Conference basement.

After winning their first Stanley Cup in 20 years, the Carolina Hurricanes entered this season facing the challenge of repeating as champions.

Dropping their first two games to the Florida Panthers and Washington Capitals sparked concerns that the Hurricanes were suffering from the dreaded "Stanley Cup hangover," the result of a shortened offseason followed by an even shorter preseason.

However, the Hurricanes quickly put those concerns to rest with a seven-game win streak . Granted, those wins came against weaker competition like the rebuilding Vancouver Canucks and Chicago Blackhawks, the inconsistent Montreal Canadiens, and the struggling Philadelphia Flyers.

Nevertheless, the defending champs defeated teams they were expected to beat, stockpiling much-needed points as they climbed into first place in the overall standings, where they've been since Oct. 20.

Their championship roster remains largely intact , led by veteran stars Sebastian Aho, Andrei Svechnikov, Nikolaj Ehlers, and Jaccob Slavin, along with young guns Jackson Blake and Logan Stankoven. Their improved depth enabled them to offset injuries to core players like Seth Jarvis and Taylor Hall.

Any concerns that their shortened offseason would affect their aggressive forechecking and stifling defensive game have been put to rest. They're third in goals-per-game (3.79), possess the fourth-best goals-against per game (2.36), while their power play and penalty killing are among the league's best.

It remains to be seen how the Hurricanes fare as they face tougher opposition as the season goes on. Nevertheless, they've served early notice that they intend to repeat as Stanley Cup champions.

For over a decade, NHL goals-per-game averages have been rising. From 2.65 during the lockout-shortened 2012-13 season, it climbed to 3.14 by 2022-23. Those numbers dipped over the following three seasons but remain high at 3.09 in the opening month of this season.

Meanwhile, save percentages have been dropping. From a high of .915 in 2015-16, they've been steadily decreasing, reaching .896 last season and .893 during the first month of 2026-27.

It wasn't that long ago that a goalie with a save percentage below .910 was considered past their prime or good enough for backup duty. Today, it's not uncommon for starters to have save percentages hovering near .900.

Sportsnet's Justin Bourne explained several factors behind this trend. Shooters are getting better, while goalies have become predictable in their positioning. Shots are counted differently, puck possession is more valued than before, and goalies face more screened shots.

Bourne noted the widespread use of composite sticks by today's skaters bring more flexibility into their shots. He also pointed out that shooters are more creative, taking shots from angles once believed too difficult to score.

The butterfly style of goaltending has been universally adopted, bringing what Bourne called more structure to the position. However, it's also made it easier for shooters to anticipate their moves.

By the end of last season, eight goalies with at least 25 games played had save percentages over .910. During the opening month of this season, 11 goalies with at least five starts have save percentages over .910.

Given the current direction of save percentage and goals-per-game stats, those numbers likely won't improve as the season progresses.

Winner: The Edmonton Oilers' Leading Scorers

When a team carries the NHL's top two scorers since 2015-16 , and one of the highest-scoring defensemen since 2021-22 , they're going to generate lots of offense.

Edmonton Oilers forwards Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and defenseman Evan Bouchard haven't disappointed their fans with their scoring abilities. However, the pace they've been on to open this season hasn't been seen in the NHL for decades.

Since the Oilers' 6-5 overtime loss in their opening match against the Vancouver Canucks on Sept. 29, McDavid, Draisaitl, and Bouchard have been tearing it up offensively, carrying their club to an 8-2-2 record and third place in the Western Conference standings as of Oct. 28.

Bouchard led all defensemen during that period with seven goals and 21 points in 12 games. At his current pace, he would reach 147 points over 84 games , eclipsing Bobby Orr's single-season record of 139 points.

Draisaitl was second among league scorers with 12 goals and 24 points in 12 games. He's on pace to reach 168 points, which would break his previous career high of 128 points in 2022-23.

McDavid, meanwhile, had a league-leading 26 assists and 34 points. He's on pace for the greatest single-season performance ever. At his current pace, he would finish with over 182 assists and 238 points , topping Wayne Gretzky's single-season records for assists (163) and points (215).

It remains to be seen if McDavid, Draisaitl, and Bouchard can maintain their current level of production. Most likely, their pace will drop over the grind of a long season. Nevertheless, the three Oilers superstars have had one of the most memorable months for NHL scorers in a long time.

articles.title: Why is WWE Wasting Gunther After Retiring John Cena and AJ Styles?
articles.summary: 2025 ended with an emphatic statement, declaring Gunther the biggest heel in WWE with a dominant win over John Cena to send him into retirement.
articles.body:
2025 ended with an emphatic statement, declaring Gunther the biggest heel in WWE with a dominant win over John Cena to send him into retirement.

To start the year, The Ring General taunted until AJ Styles stepped up and put his career on the line at Royal Rumble 2026, allowing Gunther to retire another legend.

That same night, Gunther was also the runner-up in the men's Rumble match, solidifying his direction toward top gold once again in the new year.

It is now October, and The Career Killer is the least relevant he has been in his main-roster run, feuding with Finn Bálor and Danhausen on SmackDown. What happened to Gunther?

After Royal Rumble, Gunther ran into an angry Dragon Lee, looking to avenge his retired friend AJ Styles.

This feud had some heat, but WWE never planned for Dragon to look like a serious threat to The Career Killer. Gunther would defeat and unmask Dragon, who would simply accept that loss.

This left Gunther without any direction into WrestleMania 42 until he abruptly revealed he was helping Paul Heyman to fight Seth Rollins.

Gunther did defeat Rollins at 'Mania, but the match was focused more on the return of Bron Breakker, transitioning The Visionary to another feud.

The Career Killer was already so lost that WWE decided to move him to SmackDown for a fresh start.

Gunther would quickly go after WWE champion Cody Rhodes, earning a shot at the champion at Clash in Italy.

The Career Killer lost to The American Nightmare but with controversy since Gunther's leg was under the bottom rope.

Less than three weeks later on SmackDown, the two fought again, but special guest referee Sami Zayn cost Gunther the match then caused a disqualification in the restarted contest.

At Night of Champions, Zayn pinned Rhodes to take the WWE Championship, going on to lose the title to CM Punk eight days later on Raw.

Time and again, The Career Killer lost without gaining any heat. His wins over John Cena and AJ Styles felt like a distant memory.

Twice after Royal Rumble, WWE teased the possibility of Gunther retiring someone else.

During his brief alliance with Paul Heyman, all signs pointed to Gunther eventually challenging Brock Lesnar. Instead, The Beast Incarnate chose Oba Femi as his final opponent.

Instead into SummerSlam, WWE set up Gunther vs. Nick Aldis. The general manager stepped out of his authority role to fight in a WWE ring for the first time.

All signs pointed to Gunther retiring Aldis after his first WWE match. Instead, despite The Career Killer winning, the talking point of the night was that Aldis looked good enough to wrestle multiple times in the future.

As a consolation, Aldis threw Gunther in a No. 1 contender match on Night 2 of SummerSlam. Kevin Owens would go on to win that contest and leave The Career Killer with no real direction since.

While Gunther has regularly appeared on television since SummerSlam, it barely feels like The Career Killer matters to the current product.

He is ostensibly feuding with Finn Bálor, but that story has gone nowhere since the two both failed to win triple threat matches that could have led them to another WWE Championship opportunities.

Instead of heating up this feud, WWE has forced Danhausen into the mix, who Gunther has been scheduled to fight twice in October despite he and The Prince never fighting one on one.

Unless the end goal is Gunther retiring The Prince at the end of this story, which is likely too early for Bálor, this rivarly would need to massively heat up quick to be worth the time wasted.

At this point, The Career Killer is no longer amongst the most hated heels in WWE, and no one has fought recently has cared that he retired any legends in the past year.

It is likely that WWE had to pivot from the original plan to continue the dominance of Gunther.

Rey Mysterio is close to retirement and was likely a potential opponent for Gunther, but it is hard to imagine The Master of the 619 would want anyone but his own son Dominik Mysterio ending his career.

Brock Lesnar was an obvious opponent for Gunther to retire at SummerSlam, but Oba Femi was served much better by his role in Lesnar's retirement.

Both cases show though that it is better not to give one wrestler every legend's retirement.

It would have been best to play off the heat of retiring Cena by pitting The Career Killer against Cena's friends.

Instead, he mean-mugged at CM Punk once, and his eventual feud with Cody Rhodes was not focused at all on the end of Cena's career.

Gunther should have been a big problem for the top stars in WWE on his way to recapturing the world title.

Instead, he lost repeatedly and fell out of focus in an increasingly crowded world title scene on SmackDown.

WWE has no path forward to get Gunther back to the heat he held coming into 2026, but that does not mean The Career Killer is lost entirely.

This feud with Finn Bálor needs to get personal, and the two must get a major spotlight for their singles match to come. It would be best if it led to multiple big matches.

Whoever wins that feud should immediately join the WWE Championship picture, which would make more sense for The Prince given the current heel champion.

However, WWE cannot lose track of Gunther again. He should transition to another feud that he can win on the road to the next WrestleMania.

The Career Killer gimmick may have played itself out as there are no obvious legends left for Gunther to retire, but there are plenty of fresh feuds for him on SmackDown.

A world title reign in 2026 is unlikely, but WWE should make sure The Career Killer is penned in for a world title reign in 2027 if he is going to remain one of WWE's top heels.

articles.title: South Korea captain, LA star Son Heung-min backed by coach amid rift rumour
articles.summary: Robert Moreno names captain Son Heung-min in South Korea’s squad for Saudi Arabia and Qatar games despite rift rumours.
articles.body:
Son Heung-min will continue as South Korea captain despite reports of friction between the former Tottenham striker and his senior international teammates, coach Robert Moreno said.

Moreno named Son, now 34 and playing for LAFC in Major League Soccer, in his squad for friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Qatar next month.

He also selected experienced Europe-based trio Kim Min-jae, Hwang Hee-chan and Hwang In-beom, who reports say were ready to quit the national team last month.

Moreno said he had held “many conversations with the players” since taking over on an interim basis after South Korea’s World Cup flop in North America.

“I spent more time communicating than training,” the Spaniard said at a news conference on Thursday that lasted more than an hour.

“Even in the best teams, people can have different opinions. What matters is how those differences are resolved.”

Moreno’s contract is set to expire after the two friendlies, although South Korean football chiefs could keep him on for the Asian Cup, scheduled for Saudi Arabia in January.

When asked about Son’s leadership role in the team, Moreno said: “The captain is Son Heung-min. I have nothing more to say.”

Speculation about discord emerged after Bayern Munich defender Kim threw his boots in anger after being substituted in the second half of a 0-0 home friendly draw with Venezuela this month.

Kim said afterwards that “every player needs to put their head down and give it their all”, fuelling talk of divisions within the squad.

Moreno said “the team is healthy” and backed the players to work together.

“I believe you can find the answer in what I have said today and the squad that has been announced,” he said.

South Korea’s football association this month told fans to stop “excessive personal attacks” on players.

The national team is in the crosshairs after a poor showing at the World Cup, which saw coach Hong Myung-bo quit after they failed to get past the group stage.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé’s global brand takes a hit as three Chinese sponsors pull back amid growing boycott pressure
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé has lost three Chinese sponsors within hours after a viral video clip upset audiences in China.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé has lost three Chinese sponsors within hours after a viral video clip upset audiences in China. Dongpeng Beverage, Mengniu and Milkground all ended their deals this week, according to Forbes. The trigger was a French online show, where the Real Madrid forward picked a meme that placed his face on a figure he called a Chinese dictator. China's state broadcaster has also paused La Liga coverage tied to him. Mbappé has since apologised, but L'Équipe says the apology will change nothing for his Chinese partners.Mbappé loses three Chinese sponsors after meme remarkThe clip came from The Bridge, a French online show. Asked which meme about himself he liked most, Mbappé chose an edit that put his face on a man he described as a Chinese dictator. He named no one. The version that spread fastest shows his face on a portrait of Mao Zedong. The original footage has since been taken down, though fans had already recorded it.The business response came within hours. Dongpeng Beverage, whose Bu Shui La electrolyte drink carried Mbappé's face on bottles and adverts, ended its deal with immediate effect. It cited zero tolerance for behaviour that offends national sentiment. Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, issued an almost identical statement. Cheese maker Milkground followed.Dior, Hublot and On also pulled his content from their Weibo pages, the Global Times reported.What the lost deals are worthGoal, citing L'Équipe, says two of the contracts were worth about €7 million a year combined. Those were the Mengniu deal and one with an energy drink firm it calls Buxuela, which may be the same company Forbes names as Dongpeng. They were due to run until February and March 2027, and renewal looked highly likely. Now it won't happen.Forbes estimates Mbappé will earn $100 million this season, with $30 million from endorsements and business interests. None of the Chinese companies disclosed what they paid him, so the size of the hit to that $30 million is unclear.He apologised in a statement on Tuesday, saying he now realises his remark "hurt the feelings of many in China" and among Chinese communities worldwide. He said that was never his intention and that he holds deep respect for the Chinese people and their history.Fallout for On, La Liga and Real MadridThe larger exposure may belong to On. Mbappé ended a 20-year relationship with Nike this year to sign with the Swiss brand, and Forbes reports he took an equity stake. China is a major market for On, so his standing there is no longer only about appearance fees. The company had not commented by Tuesday.La Liga has its own problem. China Media Group, the parent of CCTV, has suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches involving Mbappé, according to The Paper, a Shanghai outlet cited by the Global Times. That non-exclusive deal, the league's first with the state broadcaster in nine years, covers this season, with games shown free on CCTV-5+.The bigger contract is digital. In early August, Javier Tebas signed a deal in Beijing making Migu, the streaming service owned by China Mobile, the league's exclusive new media partner in mainland China through 2029-30. Migu shows all 380 matches a season. It is also state owned, and whether it follows CCTV is what La Liga will be watching this week.Real Madrid have been here before. A 30 August post about flood victims in "Nepal and Tibet" was deleted on 3 September after the Global Times pushed for different wording, and a February post by Dean Huijsen needed an apology on Weibo.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn Is the Payoff to One of WWE's Greatest Stories Ever Told
articles.summary: When Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn take to the squared circle in a battle of world champions at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday, November 7, it will not only serve as the main event of a premium live event, but also the latest chapter in one of the greatest stories the pro wrestling empire has ever produced.
articles.body:
When Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn take to the squared circle in a battle of world champions at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday, November 7, it will not only serve as the main event of a premium live event, but also the latest chapter in one of the greatest stories the pro wrestling empire has ever produced.

It is a story four years in the making, originating in 2022, seemingly culminating a year later, and revisited here as both men stand atop their respective brands as the top dogs of Raw and SmackDown, respectively.

In 2022, Zayn was fresh off a loss to Johnny Knoxville at WrestleMania 38 and lacking direction. He joined up with The Bloodline as an unofficial member of the faction, interfered in nearly all of their matches, and proved his loyalty over time.

Along the way, Zayn was so entertaining and lovable that fans bonded with him. There was genuine emotion as they followed his story, from an independent conspiracy theorist to "Sami Uso," finally accepted by the group he had tagged along with for months.

At the 2023 Royal Rumble, Zayn had grown tired of being treated like dirt by Reigns, berated and verbally assaulted. Faced with blasting his friend, Kevin Owens, with a steel chair, Zayn answered one last belittlement with a chair across the back of the Tribal Chief in one of the truly great moments in modern WWE history.

The crowd erupted for Zayn that night, and a few weeks later in Montreal, they were rabidly behind him as he battled Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. He fell short of capturing the title then, thanks to interference from the Usos. Still, he would avenge the entire Bloodline experience at WrestleMania 39 when he teamed with Owens to defeat The Usos in the main event of Saturday's broadcast.

Zayn would agree to set aside their past issues and join forces with The Bloodline and CM Punk for the main event of the 2024 Survivor Series: War Games.

Since that point, though, the beloved Zayn's babyface run got stale and the fans betrayed him, began booing him, and necessitated a heel turn. As he has done countless times throughout his career, Zayn embraced the new role and did everything in his power to make the most of the Last Real Good Guy, obliviously claiming to be the same hero they cheered for all of those years and that it was the fans who betrayed him.

He has been so entertaining in the role that he is now a two-time WWE champion and the centerpiece of the SmackDown brand, a well-deserved spot for a guy who has consistently proven capable of getting (and staying) over.

When he squares off with Reigns in Riyadh at Crown Jewel, he will do so not as The OTC's lackey, looking to upset him for the championship, but as a cunning and fully realized WWE main eventer with the very real possibility of defeating the face of the company in a high-profile champion vs. champion match, a fitting conclusion to their epic story.

Reigns, as he did entering Elimination Chamber, has mistakenly underestimated Zayn, brushed him off, and tried to diminish the significance of his title and status as champion.

Even as a babyface, the leader of the Bloodline does not respect Zayn as his equal, which is true to the story and the character. The question is whether he will live to regret that attitude.

Or, perhaps, he is the dominant Superstar. Maybe Reigns steamrolls Zayn ahead of Survivor Series: War Games and what is expected to be The Bloodline's date with 946 inside the titular match.

Speaking of which, maybe a Zayn victory comes as a result of Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Carmelo Hayes, and Jaida Parker making an unscheduled stop in Riyadh.

The match does not need it, but it may be the only way Zayn picks up the win and, in his mind, silences the doubters and, well, finishes his story.

articles.title: What injury details did Kirill Marchenko reveal to a fan before the Toronto Maple Leafs received an update
articles.summary: Toronto Maple Leafs forward Kirill Marchenko shares his two-week recovery expectation for a lower-body injury ahead of the team's official announcement. Fans eagerly await confirmation as he becomes a key player in their offense.
articles.body: Toronto Maple Leafs forward Kirill Marchenko reportedly told a fan he expected to return from a lower-body injury in about two weeks, following an encounter at Calgary’s airport. The reported timeline emerged before Toronto announced that the winger would be out week-to-week, leaving fans awaiting further details about his recovery.Marchenko was injured during the Maple Leafs’ game against the Calgary Flames on Monday. His absence is a concern for Toronto after he made an encouraging start to his time with the team.Kirill Marchenko shares Toronto Maple Leafs injury timelineKirill Marchenko reportedly told a fan at Calgary’s airport that he expected to return in approximately two weeks, but the Toronto Maple Leafs’ official update described his status as week-to-week. The two-week estimate came from the fan’s account and should not be treated as a confirmed medical timeline.A fan identified as Mikel Wilson posted on X that he encountered Marchenko at Calgary’s airport on Tuesday. According to Wilson, the forward was heading home early and said he expected to be back in about two weeks. Wilson also described Marchenko as friendly and shared a photo from their meeting.The post attracted attention from hockey fans, with many reacting to the unusual source of the update. However, a reported conversation at an airport is not the same as an official medical statement from the player or team.How did Kirill Marchenko suffer his injury?Marchenko was hurt during the Maple Leafs’ game against the Calgary Flames on Monday. The supplied report states that he became tangled with Calgary forward Yegor Sharangovich early in the second period and fell awkwardly.He appeared to favor his knee while making his way to the bench. Toronto announced during the third period that he had sustained a lower-body injury and would not return to the game. Head coach Jim Hiller did not provide further details after the contest.The team later classified Marchenko as week-to-week, indicating that he was expected to miss time but without specifying a confirmed date for his return.Why is Marchenko’s absence significant for Toronto?Marchenko had made a strong start with the Maple Leafs after arriving from the Columbus Blue Jackets in a reported trade involving Matthew Knies. According to the supplied report, he recorded 14 points, including six goals and eight assists, in his first 13 games with Toronto.That early production made him an important contributor to the team’s offense. His absence could require adjustments to Toronto’s forward combinations and scoring options while he recovers.For now, the key distinction is between the fan-reported estimate and the official injury designation, and the reported two-week timeframe may offer a hopeful indication, but the Maple Leafs have not confirmed when Marchenko will return.
