articles.title: Georgia's extended deal with Learfield 'one of largest' in college athletics
articles.summary: Georgia athletics extended its partnership with Learfield, its multimedia partner, through 2042 to boost revenue and athlete marketing.
articles.body:
Georgia athletics has struck a new deal with Learfield, its multimedia rights partner, that will run through 2042.

The school isn't disclosing financial terms but on Thursday called it "one of the largest revenue-generating relationships in college athletics."

In 2017, Georgia entered into a 10-year, $152.5 million deal with IMG College and JMI Sports. IMG College and Learfield merged in 2018 and has been known as Learfield since 2021.

Georgia was initially set to make at least $15.7 million in 2026-2027, but the school lists its multimedia revenue for the fiscal year at $18.3 million in figures provided to UGA's athletic board last month.

Ohio State announced a new deal with Learfield earlier this year that was built on a revenue-sharing model that brought more to the school as Learfield generated more money from sponsorships and media, according to 247Sports.

Georgia extended its partnership with Learfield for 15 years.

"The agreement aligns with Georgia Athletics' aggressive revenue growth strategy and expands the ability to collaborate on new sponsorship, media and fan engagement opportunities," UGA said in its announcement. "Through the partnership, Georgia continues to strengthen its position as a leader in student-athlete influencer marketing campaigns, sponsorships, and brand partnerships."

The college space has changed dramatically in recent years and Learfield has become a major player in third-party NIL deals for athletes.

"To remain at the forefront during this new era in college athletics, it is vitally important we strengthen our investment in student-athletes and connect them with brands that help them be successful during their time at UGA and beyond," Georgia athletic director Josh Brooks said in a statement. "Learfield is the industry leader when it comes to fostering strategic partnerships, and we are thrilled to extend our agreement for the next 15 years."

Among schools who Learfield partners with, according to the Sports Business Journal, are Alabama, Tennessee, Texas, Michigan, Oregon and Oklahoma.

Learfield and Georgia Bulldog Sports Marketing played roles in the on-field corporate logos at football with Progressive and softball with Georgia's Own Credit Union and partnerships with brands like Coca-Coloa, Delta Airlines, Chick-fil-A and more.

Learfield is headquartered in Dallas. Private equity firm TPG is finalizing the purchase of Learfield to make it the majority owner, SBJ reported.

Georgia collaborated with Learfield Impact services to set up athlete marketing deals with brands like DoorDash and Jersey Mikes and facilitated brand activations with Learfield and UGA's media team. Its work also includes enhanced fan experiences and revenue growth with digital fan engagement, ticketing, marketing and fundraising.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin fumes over Alabama kickoff time, accuses SEC of not wanting LSU to win
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin says he never considered Alabama vs. LSU wouldn't be a night game, joking the SEC may be punishing him after recent legal battles.
articles.body: The Week 10 SEC football schedule will feature a mid-afternoon kickoff when Alabama visits LSU. Both conference rivals are on a bye this week, having entered the break ranked in the top 25. The 3:30 p.m. kickoff was apparently less than ideal for LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. "I never even considered that it wouldn't be at night," Kiffin said when asked Wednesday about next week's game. Alabama-LSU has become a nighttime staple in recent years. The rivalry game has been played at night in each of the past six seasons, while the last non-night meeting in Baton Rouge came in 2010. "I didn't even think to think about the time," Kiffin said. "I just assumed, especially since the last 16 years, this game has been at night here all the time. I guess that's probably naive of me." DEION SANDERS CRUSHED OVER ALLEGATIONS OF PAYING OFF MEDIA CRITIC Ole Miss, where Kiffin coached for six seasons, is scheduled to play Georgia in a Primetime game on November 7. Against the backdrop of legal disputes involving Kiffin, LSU and the SEC, the LSU coach suggested the league office may have viewed the scheduling decision as an opportunity to punish him. "I was joking to [LSU SID Michael Bonnette] earlier, saying obviously the SEC wanted to change it from how it's been to give LSU less of an advantage because of how well LSU plays at night and how intimidating it is to play here," Kiffin said. "I was like, 'If someone thinks the SEC wants us to win this year after what's been going on, they must've just been on Mars the last four months.'" articles.title: Jake Paul to return from broken jaw for Christmas Eve boxing bout
articles.summary: Jake Paul will return to boxing for the first time since he sustained a broken jaw on Dec. 24 in Dubai, Most Valuable Promotions announced Thursday.
articles.body:
Oct. 29 (UPI) -- Jake Paul will return to boxing for the first time since he sustained a broken jaw on Dec. 24 in Dubai, Most Valuable Promotions announced Thursday.

Paul, who sustained jaw fractures during a loss to Anthony Joshua on Dec. 19 in Miami, underwent multiple surgeries to address the issue. His next opponent will be announced at a later date.

"We've got plenty of names on the list," Paul said in a statement . "Let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out."

Paul (12-2) won the first six bouts of his career. He took his first loss -- by split decision -- in 2023 to Tommy Fury. Paul went on to win his next six bouts before his loss to Joshua.

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face," Paul said. "Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

"I'm hungrier than ever and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

Earlier this month, Paul released a list of desired future matchups , including potential opponents Canelo Alvarez, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder and Ryan Garcia, among others.

articles.title: Week 9 college football best bets: Northwestern, Wisconsin lead road-heavy card
articles.summary: Ohio State visits USC without Julian Sayin, and Oregon hosts No. 20 Northwestern.
articles.body:
Six of the seven picks on the Week 9 college football best bets card back road teams, including No. 20 Northwestern , which visits an Oregon team that just lost Dante Moore for the season and fired its offensive coordinator.

No. 2 Ohio State lays 6.5 points at USC in its first full game without Julian Sayin. No. 25 Wisconsin gets 3.5 at Iowa, where the Badgers haven't won since 2018. Every game on the card also carries a total pick, and four of them are unders.

Hat tip to Game On Paper and ESPN FPI for providing a lot of the advanced stats and matchup data.

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 12 p.m. ET, Fox

No. 25 Wisconsin (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) beat No. 16 USC 24-7, the Badgers' first regular-season win over the Trojans in program history . Wisconsin held USC to minus-17 rushing yards and sacked the quarterback five times. The defense had to carry the game because Colton Joseph threw for only 58 yards.

Iowa (5-2, 2-2) has won the last four meetings in the series, including a 37-0 win in Madison last season. Badgers coach Luke Fickell knows the Hawkeyes will test his front differently than USC did. Against Iowa, he said, "it's going to be a completely different challenge for us to stop the run."

Iowa's offense, however, is in its worst shape of the season. The Hawkeyes lost 13-10 at Minnesota after Jeremy Hecklinski was pulled in the second quarter, and Hank Brown will start Saturday. Leading rusher Kamari Moulton is also out for the season. Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz called the quarterback play "not good enough" and said, "Neither one of them are really experienced right now."

Wisconsin allows 4.15 yards per play, so an Iowa offense without its top back and with an unsettled quarterback shouldn't build a two-score lead. Iowa still averages 28 points per game, and a 20-17 final clears 36.5.

Picks: Wisconsin 20-17, Wisconsin +3.5, O36.5

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 12:45 p.m. ET, SEC Network

No. 12 Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2 SEC) came back from 21 points down at Texas to tie the game at 24 but lost 34-27. Trinidad Chambliss went 25 of 52 for 250 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions. One of those picks came on fourth-and-goal from the Texas 2 just before halftime.

Texas running back Raleek Brown ran for 157 yards on 23 carries against the Rebels, who bring the SEC's worst run defense into this game. Auburn has a quarterback built to test that weakness. Byrum Brown leads the Tigers with 480 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he hasn't turned the ball over in two straight games against Georgia and LSU.

Auburn (4-3, 2-3) lost 38-17 to LSU last week. Still, this is the same team that won at No. 1 Georgia earlier this month, and Ole Miss is its fourth straight ranked opponent. Tigers coach Alex Golesh called the Rebels a "really well-coached football team and, in a big way, a football team that knows how to win ."

Auburn averages 5.66 yards per carry, so its ground game can sustain drives and keep the Ole Miss offense on the sideline. Those longer possessions keep Auburn within two touchdowns and push the total below 57.5.

Picks: Ole Miss 31-24, Auburn +13.5, U57.5

Kansas State (+1.5) vs. Colorado (U46.5)

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 2 p.m. ET, TNT

Kansas State (4-3, 1-3 Big 12) is likely to start its third different quarterback in three weeks. Avery Johnson is out again with an undisclosed injury. Jacob Knuth went 26 of 41 for 194 yards in last week's 28-17 loss at Arizona State and is listed as doubtful . The Wildcats led that game 17-14 in the second half before the Sun Devils scored twice late.

Colorado (2-5, 0-4) is in worse shape. The Buffaloes have lost five straight. Last week they led Oklahoma State 24-23 at halftime, then were outscored 34-0 and held to 120 second-half yards in a 57-24 loss. Coach Deion Sanders said his team's lone constant has been penalties: "That's the only thing we're consistent in is getting penalties , and that doesn't make sense to me."

Colorado averages just 4.04 yards per carry, and quarterback Isaac Wilson lost a fumble on a keeper in Stillwater. The Buffaloes' defense is good enough to slow a Wildcats offense led by a backup, so the under is the safer side.

K-State has also beaten Sanders' teams in each of the last two seasons, including a 31-28 win in Boulder in 2024. A Colorado offense that can't run and keeps giving the ball away hands a short-handed Kansas State team enough chances to win a low-scoring game.

Picks: Kansas State 24-20, Kansas State +1.5, U46.5

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Peacock

No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten) has won four straight. Last week the Wildcats forced three turnovers and recorded four sacks in a 42-14 win over Rutgers. Quarterback Aidan Chiles has 1,617 passing yards, 12 touchdowns, one interception and nine rushing scores. Northwestern's offense is run by Chip Kelly, who was Oregon's head coach from 2009 to 2012.

Oregon (4-3, 2-2) was shut out in the second half of its loss to Illinois. Ducks coach Dan Lanning then fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. He also ruled out Dante Moore for the rest of the year, saying, "I'm not anticipating him being back this season."

Jay Johnson takes over play-calling. Oregon has turned the ball over 10 times in its last three games while Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have split starts. Wildcats coach David Braun said the coordinator firing "does certainly put a unique twist on this week's preparation."

Northwestern ranks eighth nationally in adjusted offensive EPA per play, while Oregon ranks 104th. The Ducks' defense still has Matayo Uiagalelei, who is second in the Big Ten with 6.0 sacks, so this projects as a low-scoring game. In that kind of game, the team that protects the ball has the advantage, and Northwestern has done that better than Oregon.

Picks: Northwestern 24-20, Northwestern +3.5, U47.5

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, ESPN

No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) has the nation's longest active winning streak after a 21-13 win over Houston. Devon Dampier ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns in that game. He also threw two interceptions for the second straight week, including one on a drive with Utah up a point in the fourth quarter .

Cincinnati (5-2) ended a two-game skid by upsetting No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24, its first home win over a top-10 team since 2006. JC French IV threw a career-high four touchdown passes, and Cole Tabb ran for 173 yards. Tabb leads the Big 12 at 9.6 yards per carry. Utes coach Morgan Scalley said, "Their offense is humming right now ."

Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield sees a Utah offense that stays ahead of the chains. "They don't really have many negative plays ," he said.

Utah averages 478.4 yards and 221 rushing yards per game, and Cincinnati allows 6.21 yards per play. Tabb gives the Bearcats enough offense to help push the total over 56.5. Still, Utah should finish more drives, and the Utes win by more than a touchdown if Dampier avoids giving away possessions.

Oklahoma State (-9.5) vs. Iowa State (O57.5)

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 7 p.m. ET, FS1

No. 24 Oklahoma State (5-2, 3-1 Big 12) trailed Colorado 24-23 at halftime and won 57-24. Drew Mestemaker threw for 386 yards and four touchdowns, his sixth straight 300-yard game. He also leads FBS with 41 completions of 20 yards or more. "I thought offensively we were in rhythm pretty much the whole entire game," Cowboys coach Eric Morris said.

Iowa State (3-4, 1-3) lost 39-3 at No. 25 Arizona, and first-year coach Jimmy Rogers benched Jaylen Raynor at halftime. Raynor will still start Saturday. "If you have some guys that haven't had a ton of experience, it's better off to have a guy that knows every moving piece ," Rogers said.

The Cyclones allow 7.81 yards per dropback, and Mestemaker should find receivers downfield on that defense. Iowa State's offense has its own problems: it converts just 29.4% of its third downs, which ranks 134th nationally.

Oklahoma State is 6-1 against the spread and averages 40 points per game. Iowa State should still score enough at home to push the total past 57.5, but the Cyclones don't have an offense that can keep up with Mestemaker for four quarters.

Picks: Oklahoma State 38-24, Oklahoma State -9.5, O57.5

Kickoff: Saturday, October 31, 7:30 p.m. ET, NBC

No. 2 Ohio State (6-1) plays its first full game since Julian Sayin injured his throwing arm in the 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17. Coach Ryan Day said the Buckeyes are planning to play through the postseason without Sayin. Day hasn't chosen between true freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. "Both guys had a good week of practice and both will be ready to play," Day said.

Fahey replaced Sayin at Indiana and is 9 of 13 for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions this season. USC (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) dropped out of the AP Top 25 after running for minus-17 yards in a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin. Trojans coach Lincoln Riley said, "We flat-out didn't play good enough on any of the three sides of the ball ."

USC's defense ranks 125th in adjusted EPA per play, which gives a freshman quarterback a favorable first start. Ohio State's defense allows 4.18 yards per play and 4.47 yards per dropback, and it should keep USC from scoring enough to cover. The Buckeyes don't need to throw much to win by more than a touchdown, so the game should stay under 51.5.

Picks: Ohio State 31-20, Ohio State -6.5, U51.5

articles.title: Ja’Marr Chase, Lamar Jackson & more fantasy football injury updates for Week 8
articles.summary: Key fantasy football injury updates heading into Thursday of Week 8.
articles.body:
Week 8 of the NFL season is bringing several important injury developments for fantasy football managers, with Ja'Marr Chase, Lamar Jackson, Matthew Golden, DJ Moore, Emeka Egbuka and Aaron Jones among the biggest names to monitor.

Wednesday's practices provided some encouraging developments, but there are still plenty of questions that could impact fantasy lineups heading into the weekend.

Ja'Marr Chase absence raises concern while Lamar Jackson returns

Ja'Marr Chase was not spotted during the portion of Wednesday's Cincinnati Bengals practice open to the media, an unexpected development considering he did not appear to suffer an injury during the team's Week 7 win over Baltimore. Chase caught five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in that game and has 32 receptions for 351 yards and five touchdowns through six games this season.

The lack of clarity surrounding Chase is something fantasy managers will want to monitor closely. If he is dealing with an issue that ultimately keeps him out against Tennessee, Tee Higgins would become a much more important part of Cincinnati's passing game.

Lamar Jackson provided a much more encouraging update for fantasy managers. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback was spotted in uniform and jogging onto the field at the beginning of Wednesday's practice as he works his way back from an ankle injury. Jackson has missed three consecutive games, making his return to practice a major development ahead of Baltimore's Week 8 matchup with Buffalo.

Jackson's eventual participation level and his status later in the week will be critical, but getting back onto the practice field is clearly a positive step.

Golden, Moore, Egbuka and Jones remain fantasy players to watch

Matthew Golden remains questionable for Thursday night's game against Carolina because of shoulder and foot issues. Packers coach Matt LaFleur previously expressed hope that Golden would be available, but his status remained uncertain heading into Thursday. Fantasy managers will need to monitor the final inactive list before making a decision.

DJ Moore also provided a positive development Wednesday, practicing in a non-contact jersey while dealing with a shoulder injury. The NFL's official Week 8 injury report lists Moore as a limited participant, giving him a better outlook than if he had remained sidelined.

Emeka Egbuka is another receiver trending in the right direction. Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Egbuka participated in individual drills Wednesday but "needs to do more Thursday" to move closer to a return. That makes Thursday's practice especially important for his fantasy outlook.

Aaron Jones, meanwhile, did not participate in Minnesota's Wednesday practice because of his knee injury, according to head coach Kevin O'Connell. Jones is considered day-to-day, leaving fantasy managers waiting for his participation later in the week.

With so many high-profile players dealing with injuries, Thursday and Friday practices will be critical. Chase's status is one of the biggest developments to watch, while Jackson's return to practice gives fantasy managers reason for optimism.

articles.title: Will Rams be active at trade deadline? Sean McVay shares insight
articles.summary: The 49ers and Seahawks have already made big trades to help their teams, but the Rams are unlikely to follow suit.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams ' rivals have already been active ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline , with the Seattle Seahawks acquiring Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers striking a deal to bring back DeForest Buckner. Though the rest of the NFC West is making moves, don't expect the same from the Rams.

They view their trade deadline acquisitions as the eventual returns of Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Davante Adams, who are all on injured reserve.

Sean McVay was asked on Wednesday whether the Rams have had trade discussions after seeing the 49ers and Seahawks make their deals, but he suggested Los Angeles won't be active before the deadline. If those key players were ruled out for the season, it might be a different story.

"No, no, that's not something – based on our situation, the good thing for us is, what you look at is hopefully some of those trades will be guys getting back from injury that haven't played for us," McVay said. "That's the way that we look at it. Like I've told you in years past, you always think about it, but with the amount of guys that have not been available that are key and focal points for really both sides of the football, we look at those guys hopefully being able to return within a month. That's where that value lies for us. Maybe it'd be a different conversation if we're talking about guys that are on IR and done for the whole season. The good thing is a lot of the guys that are big, huge parts that we're missing, we do expect to get back at some point, just not exactly sure when that is."

The Rams have been waiting for Garrett to return from IR, as he's been eligible since Week 6. However, he didn't play the last two games, and he's already been ruled out for this coming week against the Los Angeles Chargers. McVay said they're on a "week-to-week basis" with him, admitting "it's frustrating" to not have any updates.

Ferguson is also eligible to return but isn't ready to come back yet, and Adams is expected to miss at least six weeks with a hamstring injury.

The Rams could use a wide receiver to pair with Puka Nacua in the meantime, but other than that, their roster is in good shape. The biggest concern is their special teams unit, which has been the worst in the NFL thus far.

articles.title: Exeter ready for 'outstanding' Salford - Taylor
articles.summary: The Grecians head to the North West to face a side six points clear at the top of League Two.
articles.body:
Exeter manager Matt Taylor says his side will need to be at their best if they are to get anything out of their tie against League Two leaders Salford.

The Grecians head to the AIG Stadium on Saturday to face a side who have won seven games on the bounce, including an excellent 4-2 victory away to Walsall on Monday .

However, Exeter have also been in a rich vein of form themselves, having shot up the table in the last month, winning four of the last five games.

Taylor said: "It's one we're really looking forward to, but we'll have to be at our best to get anything out of this game."

He described Salford's showing against Walsall as "outstanding".

"I think anyone who watched that game would testify to that.

"Their attacking play - some of the play which went through their team was above League Two level."

City have a lot of momentum on their side, having come off the back of a 2-1 win against Fleetwood, who just knocked Arsenal out of the League Cup .

But Taylor knows it will be a tighter matchup against Salford.

He said: "The game will turn us into a defensive team, but they've conceded goals as well this season.

"But at the end of the game I don't want to be speaking about their outstanding attacking players, which they clearly have, but about us instead."

articles.title: Dortmund's Karetsas could be fit to face 'pinnacle' Bayern, says Kovač
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovač has left open whether attacker Konstantinos Karetsas will play in the Bundesliga table topper at Bayern Munich on Saturday...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovač has left open whether attacker Konstantinos Karetsas will play in the Bundesliga table topper at Bayern Munich on Saturday.

The Greek close-season signing suffered a ligament injury during the game at Union Berlin in mid-October. He has since missed wins against Sabah, Eintracht Frankfurt and Werder Bremen in the German Cup on Tuesday.

"Kosta trained with the team in part today. The plan is for him to train with the squad tomorrow. Then we will make the decision whether he is ready for Munich or not," Kovač told a news conference on Thursday.

"The lads who played the last game are all fit."

Kovač is looking forward to the clash with his ex-side Bayern, who ran away with the title last term.

"It is the Klassiker. After a long time, we have the chance to travel to Munich level on points. That makes the game more exciting, but not easier. Bayern are the pinnacle not only in Germany but in Europe. We have to play 90 minutes at the very highest level," the 55-year-old said.

Kovač rejected criticism of a lack of consistency from his squad after a 2-0 lead was squandered in the cup, only for Marcel Sabitzer to score a late free-kick.

"There is no team in the world that dominates the opponent for 90 minutes," countered the coach, before stressing the standard required against the record champions.

"We have to play at the very highest level. We have the ambition to take something from down there (in Munich). We know it is a tough ask. But we are Dortmund."

articles.title: Bangladesh’s Shadman Islam hits century, but West Indies force collapse
articles.summary: Shadman Islam hits 100, but Jomel Warrican bags five wickets before West Indies end day two of first Test on 134-4.
articles.body:
West Indies spinner Jomel Warrican took five wickets to bowl Bangladesh out for 272 before the visitors reached 134-4 on the second day of the opening Test.

The West Indies trailed by 138 runs at stumps on Thursday, with Tagenarine Chanderpaul batting on 43 and Justin Greaves on 15 when bad light ended play early in Mirpur.

Left-arm spinner Warrican, who struck twice on Day One, returned figures of 5-53, his fourth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.

Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam, who resumed on 99 not out, reached his third Test century on the second morning but fell for 105 as Bangladesh lost their remaining seven wickets for 51 runs.

“We should have done better,” said Shadman. “If our top-order batters had converted their scores into bigger innings of 150, 170 or even 200, the team total could have reached 450 or 500.”

The hosts resumed on 213-3 and Shadman reached his hundred with a flick off debutant left-arm spinner Joshua Bishop on the second ball of the day.

But Bishop trapped him lbw in his next over to trigger a collapse.

Towhid Hridoy, who had retired hurt on 42 on the opening day due to cramps, returned to bat but was bowled by Bishop without adding to his overnight score.

Litton Das attempted to rebuild the innings with the lower order and remained unbeaten on 34, but Warrican and fast bowler Shamar Joseph dismantled the tail with Bangladesh all out before lunch.

Bishop and Joseph took two wickets each to support Warrican’s heroics.

West Indies made an aggressive start in reply, with openers John Campbell and Brandon King taking on the Bangladesh fast bowlers.

Hasan Mahmud broke through when King edged out for 15, leaving the visitors at 29-1.

Campbell continued to attack, reaching his half-century off 61 balls to take West Indies to 89-1 at tea.

The visitors resumed after a rain interruption of about an hour, but Bangladesh struck soon after play restarted.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz removed Campbell for 54 with a sharply turning off-break that took the outside edge and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto held a diving catch to his left.

“The ball was a little bit darker and we had momentum going before the rain break,” said Campbell.

“I think that [rain] allowed them to regroup and they were hitting better areas.”

Left-arm spinner Taijul Islam then struck twice in the 36th over, dismissing Kavem Hodge (7) and Amir Jangoo for a duck, to reduce the opposition to 97-4.

Chanderpaul and Greaves helped West Indies recover before bad light brought an early end to the day’s play.

articles.title: England striker Ivan Toney to face trial in 2028 over nightclub assault allegations
articles.summary: Al-Ahli forward accused of headbutting man during incident in Soho last year
articles.body:
England striker Ivan Toney will face trial over an alleged assault at a Soho nightclub in summer 2028.

The 30-year-old footballer is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London , on December 6 last year.

Toney appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday morning and formally entered a not guilty plea to a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

During the five-minute hearing, a provisional trial date was set for the same court on June 12, 2028 by Judge Christopher Hehir, who told the defendant he was "sorry" about the delay.

He said: "That's a long way in advance and I'm sorry about that. As you may know, the crown courts are operating under a great deal of pressure. We have got a massive backlog of work for various reasons."

Toney arrived at court at around 9.10am wearing black sunglasses, grey trousers and a button-up jacket over a shirt and tie.

He was released on unconditional bail after the brief hearing.

An earlier hearing was told the alleged assault happened at the 100 Wardour Street club during a confrontation between the defendant and Mr Da Silva.

It was heard the two men "squared up to each other", before Toney allegedly "lunged forward and headbutted the complainant, followed by a few punches".

The criminal case came after a Metropolitan Police investigation and the charge was announced in late July.

Toney, of Northampton, represented England at this summer's World Cup and has made 10 international appearances and scored one goal.

He missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

articles.summary: The Yankees are living rent free in Pat Murphy's head, right next to the World Series trophy.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers on the World Series last night wrapping up the greatest season in franchise history. First baseman Jake Bauers was a big part of that season, leading the team in home runs, walks and OPS during the regular season. His numbers took a big dip during the postseason, but as a free agent this winter, he's set to make a lot of money.

Manager Pat Murphy addressed this exact issue during the postgame celebration. Bauers, who secured the final out on a throw from second baseman Brice Turang, gifted the ball to his manager. Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin was streaming the celebration and caught the moment on film. Bauers and Murphy embraced and the manager basically told him not to forget about his real friends when he signs elsewhere for a lot of money.

More specifically, he told him to remember how the Brewers do things when he's on a "horse sh– Yankees team."

Bauers was out of baseball in 2024, but returned because his family needed health insurance . He played this season on a one-year deal worth $2.7 million. This offseason he should command a multi-year deal worth eight figures a year. Plus benefits.

The Brewers were middle of the pack with a $146 million payroll this season . The Yankees were third at just over $300 million. The Yankees starting first baseman this season was Paul Goldschmidt, who is also a free agent. Goldschmidt hit 18 home runs in 105 games this season.
